title: Token & Cost count does not function with a custom provider
body: ### Describe the bug When using a custom provider (Azure OpenAI via LiteLLM), tokens aren't being counted and cost isn't shown. ### Setup Please complete the following information along with version numbers, if applicable. - Windows 11 23H2 - Powershell 5.1.22621.2706 ### To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Create a crush.json with the following content: ```json { "$schema": "https://charm.land/crush.json", "providers": { "your-custom-provider": { "type": "openai", "base_url": "https://litellm.local.host/v1", "api_key": "REDACTED", "models": [ { "id": "gpt-5", "name": "GPT-5", "context_window": 400000, "default_max_tokens": 16384, "cost_per_1m_in": 1.25, "cost_per_1m_out": 10.0 }, { "id": "gpt-5-mini", "name": "GPT-5-Mini", "context_window": 400000, "default_max_tokens": 8192, "cost_per_1m_in": 0.25, "cost_per_1m_out": 2.0 } ] } }, "models": { "large": { "model": "gpt-5", "provider": "your-custom-provider" } } } ``` 2. Launch `crush` 3. Make any request 4. Token count and cost remain at 0 and $0.00 respectively. ### Expected behavior Token and cost count should match the tokens used count and the calculated cost based on cost_per_1m_in and cost_per_1m_out. ### Screenshots ### Additional context This issue does not occur with a built-in provider (i.e. using OpenAI directly using an API Key). *** **Maintainers’ note:** Formatted JSON for readability.

Updates `github.com/stretchr/testify` from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/stretchr/testify's releases.

v1.11.1

This release fixes #1785 introduced in v1.11.0 where expected argument values implementing the stringer interface (String() string) with a method which mutates their value, when passed to mock.Mock.On (m.On("Method", <expected>).Return()) or actual argument values passed to mock.Mock.Called may no longer match one another where they previously did match. The behaviour prior to v1.11.0 where the stringer is always called is restored. Future testify releases may not call the stringer method at all in this case.

What's Changed

  • Backport #1786 to release/1.11: mock: revert to pre-v1.11.0 argument matching behavior for mutating stringers by @​brackendawson in stretchr/testify#1788

title: fix: ensure it's possible to quit (`ctrl+c`) even when a dialog is open
body: This used to work in the beginning, another another fix introduced this bug. `ctrl+c` should have priority over other events and checks.

title: feat(cmd): add --prompt and --model flags; quiet mode; auto-load .env in yolo; root non-interactive run
body:
Adds first-class non-interactive usage to the root crush command:
--prompt/-p: run a single prompt and exit.
--model/-m: per-run model override (provider:model or just model).
--quiet/-q: hide spinner for scripts.
Auto-load .env in --yolo/-y mode so provider API keys (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) are picked up without manual exports.
This enables fully autonomous operation for CI/scripts and “one-shot” runs.

title: feat: LSP implementation using x/powernap
body:
Replace custom LSP client implementation with the `charmbracelet/x/powernap` library, significantly reducing codebase complexity by removing ~12,000 lines of custom LSP protocol handling code. This migration introduces:

- **Simplified client architecture**: Replace custom LSP transport, protocol, and method handling with powernap's battle-tested implementation
- **Enhanced workspace support**: Add workspace markers and inactive LSP server detection capabilities from powernap
- **Improved configuration**: Integrate powernap's default LSP server configurations and settings
- **Reduced maintenance burden**: Remove custom protocol definitions, JSON marshaling, and transport layer code
- **More features**: e.g. workspace root markers, starting LSP servers only where these files exist

The refactor maintains existing functionality while leveraging powernap's robust LSP client foundation, making the codebase more maintainable and feature-rich.

body:
This PR helps to avoid this error `Your organization must be verified to stream this model` if verifying is not possible

This PR adds a provider-level option to disable streaming while keeping the agent-facing streaming API intact.

## What

- Add disable_streaming (boolean) to ProviderConfig and schema.json.
- When enabled, baseProvider.StreamResponse performs a non‑streaming send(...) and emits exactly one EventContentDelta (full content, if any) followed by EventComplete (or a single
EventError on failure).
- Agent no longer special‑cases non‑streaming; removed the EventComplete content-append fallback. Usage tracking still runs via a.TrackUsage(...).
- Documentation in README and CRUSH.md updated with config example and clarified event behavior.
- Tests updated/added:
    - internal/llm/provider/provider_nostreaming_test.go: fallback delta+complete, fallback error, pass‑through when not disabled.
    - internal/llm/agent/agent_nostreaming_test.go: ensures we break on EventComplete even if the stream isn’t closed and content persisted via delta.

## Why

- Some providers/APIs or deployments do not support server‑sent streaming.
- Users may prefer a single final streamed result while retaining the same event-driven plumbing.
- Keeps agent/event handling consistent across modes without caller special cases.

## Details

- Default unchanged (disable_streaming: false).
- Fallback is confined to the provider layer; the agent still uses StreamResponse.

Files touched

- internal/config/config.go: add DisableStreaming to ProviderConfig.
- internal/config/load.go: propagate DisableStreaming.
- internal/llm/provider/provider.go: fallback emits delta→complete; WithDisableStreaming.
- internal/llm/agent/agent.go: remove EventComplete content fallback; always call TrackUsage.
- schema.json, README.md, CRUSH.md: docs and schema.

body:
Fixes too many open files issue

Before: Non-recursive watching - You must manually add each directory to watch and it creates thousands of file descriptors (one per directory). Leading tsystem limit to open files.

After: Recursive watching but single point uses FSEvents directly (as fsnotify but in this case it does at one shot), inotify (same thing of macos) and ReadDirectoryChangesW (it's mostly likely to be same as fsnotify)

```go
// befOre
err := fsext.WalkDirectories(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
  gw.addDirectoryToWatcher(path)  // Opens a file descriptor
})

// after
watchPath := filepath.Join(root, "...")
notify.Watch(watchPath, gw.events, events)  // 1 watch for entire tree
```

### Description

## Summary
Experiencing a transport timeout error when trying to initialize the Fetch MCP server with crush CLI. The same MCP server works fine when used outside of crush.

```
{"time":"2025-09-02T23:46:53.7299506+00:30","level":"ERROR","source":{"function":"github.com/charmbracelet/crush/internal/llm/agent.createAndInitializeClient","file":"/home/runner/work/crush/crush/internal/llm/agent/mcp-tools.go","line":342},"msg":"error initializing mcp client","error":"transport error: context deadline exceeded","name":"fetch"}
```

Current configuration in `crush.json`:

- The Fetch MCP server works correctly when used outside of crush

title: Azure OpenAI: Error "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead." when using certain models
body:
### Problem
When setting up crush CLI to use OpenAI models such as `04-mini`, `gpt5-mini`, etc. from Azure AI Foundry, the following error occurs on chat completion requests:

```
POST "https://khush-me6sc92f-eastus2.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/v1/chat/completions": 400 Bad Request
{
  "message": "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead.",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "param": "max_tokens",
  "code": "unsupported_parameter"
}
```

### Root Cause
From code search, the logic for setting `max_tokens` and `max_completion_tokens` is implemented in [`internal/llm/provider/openai.go`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/a9d3080174b8c9995555da3a1cb2bd9b71074af5/internal/llm/provider/openai.go):

- The `preparedParams` function sets either `params.MaxCompletionTokens` or `params.MaxTokens` based on the model capabilities (`CanReason`).
- For Azure OpenAI (and some new OpenAI models), the API expects `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens`.
- If the wrong parameter is sent, Azure returns an error as above.

**Relevant code:**

[openai.go#L219-L262](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/a9d3080174b8c9995555da3a1cb2bd9b71074af5/internal/llm/provider/openai.go#L219-L262)

```go
func (o *openaiClient) preparedParams(messages []openai.ChatCompletionMessageParamUnion, tools []openai.ChatCompletionToolParam) openai.ChatCompletionNewParams {
    model := o.providerOptions.model(o.providerOptions.modelType)
    // ...
    if model.CanReason {
        params.MaxCompletionTokens = openai.Int(maxTokens)
    } else {
        params.MaxTokens = openai.Int(maxTokens)
    }
    return params
}
```

### Suggested Solution
- Detect when using Azure OpenAI endpoints and always use `max_completion_tokens` for relevant models, not `max_tokens`.
- Consider model-specific and provider-specific logic for parameter naming when preparing chat completion parameters.
- Add tests to verify correct parameter is sent for both OpenAI and Azure OpenAI providers.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Set up crush CLI with Azure OpenAI endpoint and a model like `04-mini` or `gpt5-mini`.
2. Attempt to send a chat completion request.
3. Observe the error as described above.

### References
- [internal/llm/provider/openai.go](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/a9d3080174b8c9995555da3a1cb2bd9b71074af5/internal/llm/provider/openai.go)
- [Azure OpenAI API docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/reference)

### Labels
- bug
- provider: openai chatgpt
- azure

### Impact
This prevents usage of Azure OpenAI models with crush CLI until the proper parameter is used.

title: Add (discoverable) `CONTRIBUTING.md`
body:
### Description

I notice this project is taking off (nice!), and getting a lot of community contributions. At the same time it seems like the maintainers have their own ideas about how they'd like to implement features. Things are moving fast and it's not always easy for the community to understand what those ideas are. I maintain a widely used OSS project too so I totally get this - but it'd be nice to set expectations with the community to reduce the likelihood of them doing work that'll ultimately be thrown away.

Having a _discoverable_ `CONTRIBUTING.md` could help contributors:

1. Understand what types contributions are wanted
2. Understand how to make a contribution that's likely to be merged

I know now there's a Charm-wide `CONTRIBUTING.md`, but I _didn't_ know that until after I'd finished an attempt to implement a feature (https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/pull/914) and opened a PR. It's in a different repo, not in the usual `./CONTRIBUTING.md` location, and not mentioned in `README.md`. So I think there's a failure mode where someone can't learn how to contribute until they're already at the "open a PR" stage. For example I proactively looked for a `CONTRIBUTING.md` file before taking a pass at the feature but couldn't find one.

v1.10.1

🐛 Fix

  • chore: upgrade pflags v1.0.9 by @​jpmcb in spf13/cobra#2305

v1.0.9 of pflags brought back ParseErrorsWhitelist and marked it as deprecated

Full Changelog: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/compare/v1.10.0...v1.10.1

v1.10.0

What's Changed

🚨 Attention!

  • Bump pflag to 1.0.8 by @​tomasaschan in spf13/cobra#2303

This version of pflag carried a breaking change: it renamed ParseErrorsWhitelist to ParseErrorsAllowlist which can break builds if both pflag and cobra are dependencies in your project.

  • If you use both pflag and cobra, upgrade pflagto 1.0.8 andcobrato1.10.0`
  • or use the newer, fixed version of pflag v1.0.9 which keeps the deprecated ParseErrorsWhitelist

More details can be found here: spf13/cobra#2303

✨ Features

  • Flow context to command in SetHelpFunc by @​Frassle in spf13/cobra#2241

Updates `github.com/stretchr/testify` from 1.11.0 to 1.11.1
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/stretchr/testify's releases.

v1.11.1

This release fixes #1785 introduced in v1.11.0 where expected argument values implementing the stringer interface (String() string) with a method which mutates their value, when passed to mock.Mock.On (m.On("Method", <expected>).Return()) or actual argument values passed to mock.Mock.Called may no longer match one another where they previously did match. The behaviour prior to v1.11.0 where the stringer is always called is restored. Future testify releases may not call the stringer method at all in this case.

What's Changed

  • Backport #1786 to release/1.11: mock: revert to pre-v1.11.0 argument matching behavior for mutating stringers by @​brackendawson in stretchr/testify#1788

Full Changelog: https://github.com/stretchr/testify/compare/v1.11.0...v1.11.1

If you'd like to support go-colorful's development you can support me or Lucas (the original developer) through GitHub Sponsors, check out the Sponsor button up top. I also have a Ko-Fi for one-time donations.

body: ### Description I have a major usabliity issue with Crush and am wondering if there's an easy way to avoid it. During my LLM chats, it often describes something and then needs to edit a file. So it spits out the text that I need to read, but before I can read it, the "Here's what I'm going to change in the file. Allow?" dialog box pops up. See attached screenshot. At that point, I can no longer read the text behind the pop up that I _need_ to first read in order to decide whether to allow the requested edit to the file. That 'Allow edits?' dialog box should not pop up until I have finished reading what it was saying just before it popped up the dialog. Alternatively, there should be some way to still read the text behind it, and then interact with the dialog.

title: Any chance you can dispel some of the confusion around opencode?
body: Hello. I suppose this is somewhat of a bug report insofar as misleading repo history can be considered a bug. I used and enjoyed the opencode application found [here](https://github.com/sst/opencode) and [here](https://opencode.ai/). I made a mental note and then didn't use it for a week or two. After moving computers I subsequently found your archived repo [here](https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode) and was dismayed to see that the project had moved and been placed under a license less to my preference. After charm simply failed to work in nushell (unhandled panic with very little other helpful logging), I was searching for solutions when I was both irked and relieved to find that opencode was still going and was a different (ish) project than the one that was archived. Based on their assessment of the situation, it certainly looks like this name issue was meant to be misleading and that my mistake and subsequent waste of my time was precisely what was intended. It seems like you are acting in bad faith, but maybe I'm not seeing your point of view. Anyway, it would go a long way toward clearing up the misconception (and be a signal of good faith) if you would maybe drop a link and a mention to the other project in your readme. Devs like me who were confused by the repo issue would also have a better chance of seeing what happened and could choose the tool that fits their preferences better.

body:
# Crush Server-Client Architecture

This document describes the server-client architecture implemented in Crush, which enables remote access to Crush functionality through HTTP APIs.

## Overview

The server-client architecture separates Crush into two main components:

1. **Server**: A long-running HTTP server that manages Crush instances and exposes REST APIs
2. **Client**: A lightweight client that communicates with the server over HTTP

This architecture enables:
- Better resource management and isolation
- Remote access capabilities  
- Decoupling of UI from core logic
- Multi-client support
- Improved performance through persistent server instances

## Server Architecture

### Core Components

- **Server**: Main HTTP server that manages multiple Crush instances
- **Instance**: Individual Crush application instances with their own configuration and state
- **Client**: HTTP client for communicating with the server
- **Proto**: Protocol definitions and data structures for client-server communication

### Network Support

The server supports multiple network protocols:

- **Unix Domain Sockets** (Linux/macOS): `unix:///tmp/crush-{uid}.sock`
- **Named Pipes** (Windows): `npipe:////./pipe/crush-{uid}.sock`  
- **TCP** (All platforms): `tcp://host:port`

Default host is automatically determined based on the platform and user ID.

### Instance Management

Each server can manage multiple Crush instances, where each instance:
- Has a unique ID (UUID)
- Runs in a specific filesystem path
- Has its own configuration and state
- Maintains separate LSP clients and sessions
- Can be created, queried, and destroyed independently

## API Reference

The server exposes a comprehensive REST API at `/v1/` with the following endpoints:

### Health & Configuration

- `GET /v1/health` - Server health check
- `GET /v1/version` - Get server version information
- `POST /v1/control` - Server control commands (shutdown)
- `GET /v1/config` - Get server configuration

### Instance Management

- `GET /v1/instances` - List all running instances
- `POST /v1/instances` - Create a new instance
- `DELETE /v1/instances/{id}` - Delete an instance
- `GET /v1/instances/{id}` - Get instance info
- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/config` - Get instance configuration

### Session Management

- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/sessions` - List sessions for an instance
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/sessions` - Create a new session
- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/sessions/{sid}` - Get session details

### Message & History

- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/sessions/{sid}/messages` - List session messages
- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/sessions/{sid}/history` - Get session history

### Language Server Protocol (LSP)

- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/lsps` - List LSP clients and their states
- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/lsps/{lsp}/diagnostics` - Get diagnostics from specific LSP client

### Agent Operations

- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/agent` - Get agent information
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/agent` - Send message to agent
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/agent/init` - Initialize agent
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/agent/update` - Update agent model
- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/agent/sessions/{sid}` - Get agent session info
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/agent/sessions/{sid}/cancel` - Cancel agent operations
- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/agent/sessions/{sid}/prompts/queued` - List queued prompts
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/agent/sessions/{sid}/prompts/clear` - Clear queued prompts
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/agent/sessions/{sid}/summarize` - Summarize session

### Permissions

- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/permissions/skip` - Get skip requests status
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/permissions/skip` - Set skip requests status
- `POST /v1/instances/{id}/permissions/grant` - Grant or deny permissions

### Real-time Events

- `GET /v1/instances/{id}/events` - Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream for instance events

## Usage

### Starting the Server

```bash
# Start server with default settings
crush server

# Start server on specific host
crush server --host tcp://localhost:8080
```

### Client Usage

The client automatically connects to the default server or can be configured to connect to a specific server:

```bash
# Run with default server
crush

# Run with specific server host
crush --host tcp://localhost:8080
```

### Programmatic Usage

```go
// Create a client
client, err := client.DefaultClient("/path/to/project")
if err != nil {
    return err
}

// Create an instance
instance, err := client.CreateInstance(ctx, &proto.Instance{
    Path: "/path/to/project",
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

// Use the instance
sessions, err := client.ListSessions(ctx, instance.ID)
// ... work with sessions
```

## Implementation Details

### Protocol Definitions

All client-server communication uses JSON over HTTP. Key data structures are defined in `internal/proto/`:

- `Instance`: Represents a Crush instance
- `AgentMessage`: Messages sent to/from the agent
- `SessionInfo`: Session metadata and state
- `PermissionRequest`: Permission grant/deny requests
- `VersionInfo`: Server version information

### Event System

The server uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) to push real-time updates to clients:

- Agent status changes
- Session updates
- Permission requests
- LSP diagnostic updates

### Logging

The server includes structured logging with `slog` for all RPC requests and responses, making it easy to debug and monitor server operations.

### Platform-Specific Features

- **Windows**: Uses named pipes for local communication
- **Unix**: Uses Unix domain sockets for local communication
- **Cross-platform**: TCP support for remote connections

## Migration from Direct Usage

The server-client architecture is designed to be backward compatible. Existing Crush usage patterns continue to work, but now operate through the client-server model transparently.

Key changes:
- The TUI now runs as a client connecting to a server
- Multiple clients can connect to the same server
- Server instances persist between client connections
- Configuration and state are managed server-side

## Security Considerations

- Local connections (Unix sockets/named pipes) rely on filesystem permissions
- TCP connections should be used with appropriate network security measures
- Server instances are isolated by user ID and filesystem permissions
- No authentication is currently implemented for local connections

## Related Issues

- [Issue #976](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/issues/976) - Server-client architecture implementation

title: fix: support JSON objects as API keys in provider configuration
body:
## Description

This PR adds support for JSON objects as API keys in provider configurations, while maintaining full backward compatibility with string API keys.

## Problem

Some AI providers (like NEAR AI) use structured JSON objects as API keys instead of simple strings. Currently, crush fails to parse configurations with such API keys with the error:
```
json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field Config.providers.api_key of type string
```

## Solution

This change introduces a `FlexibleAPIKey` type that can handle both string and JSON object API keys:

1. **New FlexibleAPIKey type**: Custom type with JSON marshal/unmarshal methods to handle both formats
2. **Updated resolvers**: Modified to detect JSON objects and pass them through without attempting variable resolution
3. **Backward compatible**: All existing string API keys continue to work exactly as before

## Changes

- Added `internal/config/apikey.go` with the new `FlexibleAPIKey` type
- Updated `ProviderConfig.APIKey` field to use `FlexibleAPIKey` instead of `string`
- Modified resolvers to detect and preserve JSON objects
- Updated all references throughout the codebase

## Testing

- ✅ Tested with existing string API keys (e.g., `"sk-abc123"`)
- ✅ Tested with environment variable references (e.g., `"$OPENAI_API_KEY"`)
- ✅ Tested with JSON object API keys (e.g., NEAR AI's authentication object)
- ✅ All existing functionality preserved

## Example Configuration

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "nearai": {
      "type": "openai",
      "base_url": "https://api.near.ai/v1",
      "api_key": {
        "account_id": "user.near",
        "public_key": "ed25519:...",
        "signature": "...",
        "callback_url": "https://app.near.ai/sign-in/callback",
        "message": "Welcome to NEAR AI Hub!",
        "recipient": "ai.near",
        "nonce": "..."
      },
      "models": [...]
    }
  }
}
```

This configuration now works seamlessly alongside traditional string API key providers.

# 🗑️ feat(sessions): implement session deletion with auto-replacement

## 📋 Summary

Implements comprehensive session deletion functionality with confirmation dialogs and intelligent session replacement mechanism, ensuring optimal user experience when managing sessions.

## ✨ Features

### 🔐 Safe Deletion Mechanism
- **Confirmation Dialog** - Delete key triggers Yes/No confirmation dialog to prevent accidental deletion
- **Keyboard Navigation** - Support arrow keys/Tab to switch options, Y/N shortcut keys for confirmation
- **Cancel Operation** - ESC key or N key to cancel deletion operation

### 🔄 Intelligent Session Replacement
When deleting the currently active session:
- ✅ **Auto-create New Session** - System automatically creates "New Session"
- ✅ **Seamless Switching** - Automatically switches to new session, maintaining work continuity
- ✅ **Keep Dialog Open** - User remains in session management interface after deletion
- ✅ **Real-time List Updates** - Session list automatically refreshes to display new session

### 📱 User Interface Optimization
- **Intuitive Confirmation Interface** - Clearly displays information about the session to be deleted
- **Responsive Buttons** - Highlights currently selected operation
- **Consistent Interaction** - Follows application's overall UI/UX design patterns

## 🎯 User Journey

1. **Open Session Management** - User presses shortcut key to open session switcher while in current session
2. **Select Delete** - Select session to delete, press Delete key
3. **Confirm Operation** - Confirmation dialog appears showing session info and Yes/No options
4. **Intelligent Processing**:
   - **Delete Current Session** → Auto-create new session and switch to it
   - **Delete Other Session** → Normal deletion, return to session list
5. **Continue Management** - User can continue managing other sessions in the interface or close to return

## 🛠 Technical Implementation

### Modified Files:

### Key Components:
1. **SessionDeletedMsg** - Session deletion event message
2. **Confirmation Dialog** - UI component for deletion confirmation
3. **Auto-replacement Logic** - Automatic replacement logic when current session is deleted
4. **Real-time Updates** - Real-time update mechanism for session list

### Statistics:

## 🎨 UI/UX Improvements

- **Anti-accidental Design** - Requires explicit confirmation to delete sessions

- **Interface Consistency** - Confirmation dialog maintains consistency with overall app style
- **Keyboard Friendly** - Complete keyboard navigation support

## ✅ Testing & Quality

- ✅ **Compilation Passed** - No compilation errors
- ✅ **Code Quality** - Passes all linter checks
- ✅ **Functional Testing** - All scenarios for deleting current/other sessions
- ✅ **Edge Case Testing** - Cancel operations, error handling and other edge cases

## 🚀 Benefits

- **User Experience** - Safe and intuitive session management
- **Work Efficiency** - Quick deletion of unwanted sessions
- **Error Prevention** - Prevents accidental deletion of important sessions
- **Process Optimization** - Auto-creates new session after deletion, no manual operation needed

---

This feature provides a complete deletion solution for crush application's session management, balancing operational convenience and safety.

title: Option to customize coder base prompt
body:
### Description

I just discovered that you changed the OpenAI prompt to a v2 Crush prompt in the `CoderPrompt` function (related commits: 6c990b25 #1083 and 45e4e275).  

This prompt change makes the LLM **significantly less capable**, specifically:  
- It refuses to strictly follow instructions, often performing unwanted actions  
- It generates excessive `.md` files without justification  
- It produces unnecessary shell scripts and test files  
- It stubbornly avoids using sub-agents for large complex tasks  

I'm using `glm-4.5` and `qwen3-coder`, and the new prompt makes these models perform **so poorly that the degradation is immediately noticeable** after upgrading Crush.  

btw, removing the base prompt dramatically improves performance for both `glm-4.5` and `qwen3-coder`. I strongly recommend adding a configuration option in `crush.conf` to customize base prompts per model.

title: feat: add AWS bearer token authentication for Bedrock
body:
Adds support for authenticating with AWS Bedrock using bearer tokens
via the AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK environment variable. This provides
a simpler authentication method compared to full AWS credentials,
particularly useful in corporate environments.

Implementation:
- Detects when AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK is set and passes it as API key
- Bypasses the anthropic SDK's SigV4 middleware for bearer tokens
- Sets Bedrock base URL directly and uses Authorization header
- Falls back to SigV4 auth when AWS credentials are provided instead
- Maintains full backwards compatibility with existing credential auth

Changes:
- Updated hasAWSCredentials() to check for AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
- Modified Bedrock provider config to pass bearer token with "Bearer " prefix
- Enhanced anthropic client to skip bedrock middleware for bearer tokens
- Added test coverage for bearer token authentication
- Updated README with bearer token documentation and usage examples

Bearer tokens are particularly useful in corporate environments where
teams need access to Bedrock without managing AWS credentials, IAM
roles, or account-level permissions. This streamlines AI development
workflows by allowing API key-based access similar to other LLM providers.

Note: This is a temporary workaround until the anthropic SDK adds native
bearer token support. An upstream PR has been submitted to add this
functionality: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go/pull/240

References:
- https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/pull/3159
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-use.html
- https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/accelerate-ai-development-with-amazon-bedrock-api-keys/

Optionally, in the footer, use BREAKING CHANGE: followed by a detailed explanation of the breaking change. Just return the commit message, do not include any other text."
The idea is from the [Auto-generate Commit Messages with LLMs](https://hankchiu.tw/writings/auto-generate-commit-messages-with-ll-ms-in-your-terminal/) post.

title: v0.10.1: stream timeout aborts long-running reasoning tasks — request configurable stream timeout
body:
### Description
After upgrading to crush v0.10.1, I started seeing an `ERROR Stream timeout` which stops agents after roughly ~100+ seconds (model provider logs). Reverting to v0.10.0 makes the tasks complete normally. I suspect this change is related to the stream control introduced in or around issue #1070. Long-running reasoning tasks (especially with `reasoning_effort` set to `high`) require more time to produce answers and are being prematurely interrupted.

### Workaround
- Downgrading to v0.10.0 restores the previous behavior and allows the tasks to finish.

### Additional background
- It appears that some newer models (e.g., GPT-5 series) stream intermediate "thinking" content via the new Responses API, while OpenAI-compatible Chat/Completions APIs often only send the final answer (i.e., long periods of silence until completion).
- When using a model that only returns the final result via a Chat/Completions-compatible endpoint, there can be a long silence with no streamed events. That silent period can more easily trigger the stream timeout.
- Some API proxies or providers may not implement the Responses API and only proxy Chat/Completions endpoints, which means clients expecting streaming "thinking" events may see long no-output gaps.

### Suggested fixes / feature requests
- Exposing a configurable stream timeout (per-model or global)


Thanks for the great project.

### Version

v0.10.1

### Environment

CentOS 7

title: Allow Interrupting chat
body:
### Description

### Feature Request: Interrupt Running LLM/Generation

Currently, when the large language model (LLM) is running a command or generating a response, the user lacks a clear and immediate way to stop the process if it's heading in the wrong direction or taking too long.

**Proposed Solution:**
Implement support for interrupting the active operation via standard command-line methods, such as **Control+C** (or its equivalent on other platforms).

**Expected Behavior:**
1.  User starts a long-running process (e.g., a complex query, code generation).
2.  User recognizes the model is running incorrectly or that they no longer need the output.
3.  User presses **Control+C**.
4.  The running process is immediately terminated, and the user is returned to the command prompt/input line without opening a new terminal or waiting for the operation to complete.

This feature is crucial for improving user experience and productivity, especially in a command-line environment where immediate feedback and control are expected.

title: Unrecoverable API Error Loop from Malformed Response in History
body:
### Description

the issue is reported based on  v0.10.3

A malformed tool call response from the LLM can corrupt a session's history, leading to an unrecoverable loop of "400 Bad Request" errors.

When the LLM returns invalid JSON for a tool call's arguments, the application saves this corrupted data to the conversation history. On all subsequent requests in that session, this invalid history is sent back to the API, causing the server to reject the request. This renders the agent unusable for the remainder of the session.

Anthropic provider is resilent to this issue via JSON validation

However, The OpenAI and Gemini providers are remained vulnerable.

linux/gnome-terminal

when model generated a tool call with invalid JSON,
the application saved this malformed tool call into the conversation history.
on EVERY subsequent request, the API server will likely reject the request, responding with 400 Bad requests.
though this is an edge case, however, it happens quite often, espeically on those less capable models or in complex prompt

title: perf(list): optimize filter performance and limit results
body:
This commit refactors the filterable list's Filter method to improve
performance and user experience through three key changes:

1. Switch from fuzzy.Find to fuzzy.FindFrom
   - Eliminates redundant string allocations by avoiding intermediate list
   - The fuzzy library already uses strings.EqualFold internally for
     case-insensitive matching, so the pre-lowercased copy was wasted
     allocation and processing
   - Implements fuzzy.Source interface (String/Len methods) on
     FilterableList[T FilterableItem] to provide direct access to items
     without intermediate allocations

2. Remove redundant sorting
   - fuzzy.FindFrom already performs stable score-based sorting internally
   - The additional sort.SliceStable was redundant and added unnecessary
     overhead

3. Cap displayed results at 25 items
   - Prevents UI lag when filtering large lists (e.g., project-wide file
     searches with thousands of matches)
   - Benchmarking against similar tools shows comparable limits:
     * Codex: 8 items
     * Opencode: 10 items
     * Claude Code: 15 items
     * Gemini CLI: 24 items
     * Copilot CLI: 50 items
   - 25 items represents a practical middle ground that keeps the UI
     responsive while providing enough context for users to find matches

These changes, particularly 3, make crush's file search functionality much more usable in larger code base.

title: Cannot resume cancelled Crush session
body:
### Description When Crush runs an interactive command, the user may need to kill the Crush session. Such sessions may have useful context in them, but cannot always be resumed. This may be specific to Claude, which I'm using as my backend for Crush. The failure mode looks like this: ```js POST "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages": 400 Bad Request (Request-ID: req_011CTtqbEc23oMw95j8DgSwh) {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"messages.2: `tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks immediately after: toolu_0144YkqpAX8HbRbM9fq1cJPs. Each `tool_use` block must have a corresponding `tool_result` block in the next message."},"request_id":"req_011CTtqbEc23oMw95j8DgSwh"} ``` Steps to reproduce: 1. Make a temp dir. 2. Change directories to that temp dir. 3. Write a shell program that simulates "a program that never returns" ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash echo "please wait 2s" while [[ 0 ]]; do read done echo "done" ``` 4. Make it executable ```sh $ chmod 0755 ./the-tool ``` 5. Run `crush` in your workdir. 6. Ask it to run `./the-tool` 7. Crush runs the tool. The tool will never exit. 8. Press `^C` to exit Crush. 9. Fully exit Crush. 10. Re-run `crush`. 11. Press `Ctrl+S` to select a past session to resume. Resume your session. 12. Ask Crush to do anything. 13. 💥You will see the error above. The bash script included in this bug report is obviously silly¹, but bug report represents a real issue. Here's a screenshot of the interaction with some light explanation added. I had Crush write a bash script to fix these broken entries for me. When I get into the situation above, I can run the following script as ```sh $ crush-fix-orphaned-tools /path/to/directory/ (output occurs) $ crush-fix-orphaned-tools --fix /path/to/directory (fixes happen) ``` This isn't wonderful, but it allows me to continue my sessions with their context, which is what matters to me. It would be nice if Crush offered a way to resolve this error itself.
crush-fix-orphaned-tools ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail usage() { cat << 'USAGE' Fix orphaned tool_use blocks in Crush database. Usage: fix-crush-orphaned-tools /path/to/.crush [--fix] Without --fix, it will only report problems. With --fix, it will delete the problematic messages. USAGE } fix_mode=false crush_dir="" while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case "$1" in -h|--help) usage exit 0 ;; --fix) fix_mode=true shift ;; *) crush_dir="$1" shift ;; esac done if [[ -z "$crush_dir" ]]; then usage exit 0 fi # Determine database path if [[ "$crush_dir" == *crush.db ]]; then db_path="$crush_dir" elif [[ "$crush_dir" == *.crush ]] || [[ "$crush_dir" == */.crush ]] || [[ "$crush_dir" == */.crush/ ]]; then db_path="${crush_dir%/}/crush.db" else db_path="$crush_dir/.crush/crush.db" fi if [[ ! -f "$db_path" ]]; then echo "Error: Database not found at $db_path" >&2 exit 1 fi problems_found=false messages_to_delete=() # Get all sessions while IFS='|' read -r session_id title; do declare -A expected_results orphaned_tools=() orphaned_messages=() # Get all messages for this session in order while IFS='|' read -r msg_id role parts_json; do if [[ "$role" == "assistant" ]]; then # Extract tool_call IDs from assistant messages tool_call_ids=$(echo "$parts_json" | jq -r '.[] | select(.type == "tool_call") | .data.id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true) while IFS= read -r tool_call_id; do [[ -n "$tool_call_id" ]] && expected_results["$tool_call_id"]="$msg_id" done <<< "$tool_call_ids" elif [[ "$role" == "tool" ]]; then # Remove matched tool_result IDs tool_result_ids=$(echo "$parts_json" | jq -r '.[] | select(.type == "tool_result") | .data.tool_call_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true) while IFS= read -r tool_result_id; do [[ -n "$tool_result_id" ]] && unset expected_results["$tool_result_id"] done <<< "$tool_result_ids" fi done < <(sqlite3 "$db_path" "SELECT id, role, parts FROM messages WHERE session_id = '$session_id' ORDER BY created_at") # Check for orphaned tool_use blocks if [[ ${#expected_results[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then problems_found=true echo "" echo "Session: $session_id" echo "Title: $title" echo -n "Orphaned tool_use IDs: " for key in "${!expected_results[@]}"; do orphaned_tools+=("$key") orphaned_messages+=("${expected_results[$key]}") done echo "${orphaned_tools[*]}" # Get unique message IDs unique_msgs=($(printf '%s\n' "${orphaned_messages[@]}" | sort -u)) echo "Messages to delete: ${unique_msgs[*]}" if $fix_mode; then for msg_id in "${unique_msgs[@]}"; do sqlite3 "$db_path" "DELETE FROM messages WHERE id = '$msg_id'" echo " ✓ Deleted message $msg_id" done fi fi done < <(sqlite3 "$db_path" "SELECT id, title FROM sessions") if ! $problems_found; then echo "✓ No orphaned tool_use blocks found!" exit 0 elif $fix_mode; then echo "" echo "✓ Fixed all orphaned tool_use blocks!" exit 0 else echo "" echo "Run with --fix to delete these messages." exit 1 fi ```
---- ¹ The actual scenario where I encountered this was fairly mundane: I asked Crush to "open that file for me in emacs using `emacsclient`", which it obediently did. The default behavior of `emacsclient` is to tie up the command line until emacs "releases" the file, but emacs didn't recognize the buffer as a server-editing buffer, so I was unable to get emacs to "release" the `emacsclient`. ### Version `v0.10.4+dirty` installed on Ubuntu via `brew install charmbracelet/tap/crush` ### Environment Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS / terminator / tmux

title: fix: add safe agent cancellation before quit in TUI (charmbracelet/cr…
body:
This PR addresses issue #1206 by ensuring that when the user attempts to quit the TUI while an agent is busy processing tool calls, the agent operations are safely cancelled before the application exits. This prevents potential hanging processes and session corruption.

## Changes
- Modified the quit key handler in `internal/tui/tui.go` to check if the coder agent is busy
- If busy, initiates `CancelAll()` on the agent before proceeding with quit
- Adds a 2-second delay to allow cancellation to complete before exiting
- Falls back to the existing quit dialog behavior when agent is not busy

## Testing
- Verified that pressing quit (Ctrl+C) while agent is processing properly cancels operations
- Confirmed clean shutdown without hanging processes
- Existing quit behavior remains unchanged when agent is idle

title: fix(mcp): ensure command environment is set only if non-empty
body:
# Fix MCP Loading Issue with Environment Variables

## 🐛 Problem

When MCP configurations don't specify any environment variables, the `ResolvedEnv()` method returns an empty slice `[]string{}`. Setting `exec.Cmd.Env` to an empty slice causes the child process to run with **no environment variables at all**, which can cause MCP processes to fail during startup as they may depend on system environment variables like `PATH`, `HOME`, etc.

## ✅ Solution

Only set `cmd.Env` when there are actually environment variables to configure. When `ResolvedEnv()` returns an empty slice, leave `cmd.Env` as `nil` so the child process inherits the parent's environment variables.

## 🔧 Changes

**File:** `internal/llm/agent/mcp-tools.go`

```diff
- cmd.Env = m.ResolvedEnv()
+ if env := m.ResolvedEnv(); len(env) > 0 {
+     cmd.Env = env
+ }
```

### What this change does:
- Added a nil check in `createMCPTransport()` to only set `cmd.Env` when `m.ResolvedEnv()` returns a non-empty slice
- This ensures MCP processes have access to necessary system environment variables when no custom environment is specified

## 🧪 Testing

- [x] MCP clients should now start successfully even when no custom environment variables are configured
- [x] Existing functionality with custom environment variables remains unchanged
- [x] No breaking changes to the existing API

## 📝 Background

In Go's `os/exec` package:
- When `Cmd.Env` is `nil`: child process inherits parent's environment
- When `Cmd.Env` is `[]string{}`: child process gets **no** environment variables
- When `Cmd.Env` is `[]string{"KEY=value"}`: child process gets only specified variables

This fix resolves MCP loading failures that occurred when configurations didn't specify custom environment variables.

## 🎯 Impact

- **Before**: MCP processes could fail to start when no custom env vars were configured
- **After**: MCP processes inherit system environment and start reliably
- **Risk**: Low - only affects the environment variable handling logic

title: Support for Copilot's instruction files (or equivalent)
body:
## Summary

I am wondering if there's an plan for/appetite to implement support for GitHub Copilot's instructions markdown files (or a vendor-agnostic alternative, though I am not aware of any at this stage).

## Background

Most AI-assisted coding tools have support for repo-specific instruction files. There's the standard `AGENTS.md`, and then there are vendor-specific examples like `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `CRUSH.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, etc. These are great for providing a high-level view of a repository, but lack specificity.

The [`AGENTS.md`](https://agents.md) standard does allow for nested files, but then the instructions are tied directly to the hierarchy structure.

### Specific Instruction Files

GitHub Copilot has added support for tailored instruction files that complement the generic files listed above. They key differentiator is that these Markdown files have a YAML section at the top which includes an `applyTo` filter. The filter is a comma-separated glob selection. For example, to have some generic instructions apply to all Python files, and then more tailored instructions that apply _only_ to test files, one would create:

- **`.github/instructions/python.instructions.md`**

  ```markdown
  ---
  description: "Python guidelines"
  applyTo: "**/*.py"
  ---
  
  - Make sure that all public functions are thoroughly documented
  ```

- **`.github/instructions/testing.instructions.md`**

  ```markdown
  ---
  description: "Testing guidelines"
  applyTo: "tests/**/test_*.py"
  ---
  
  - Use long and description test function names.
  - Avoid docstrings, using them only explain edge cases, or other non-obvious behaviours in test functions
  ```

title: feat: allow configurable bash commands via permissions.allowed_commands
body:
Add support for configuring which bash commands are allowed through the crush.json permissions section. This allows users to enable specific commands like curl that are otherwise blocked for security reasons.

## Changes

- Add `allowed_commands` field to Permissions config
- Modify bash tool to respect allowed commands configuration  
- Update schema.json to include the new configuration option
- Update crush.json example to show curl as allowed

## Usage

Users can now add allowed commands in their crush.json:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allowed_commands": ["curl", "wget", "ping"]
  }
}
```

This maintains security by default while giving users control over specific commands they need.

Manual session naming
body:
### Description

I'd like to be able to manually set the name of a session, so that the next time I'm looking at my past sessions list, I have a better idea of what each session contains.

Right now the automatic session naming seems based off of the very first exchange with the backing model. Sometimes I'll start sessions with something like this:

```
> Use `pbpaste` to look at my clipboard. What does this mean?
🗸 Bash `pbpaste`

...(interactions happen)...
```

and get a session named `Clipboard Command in Terminal`. It would be nice to be able to rename it to `Postgresql Explain/Analyze`, so I can resume that session the next time I have an explain/analyze interaction to go through.

title: CHR-719/scrollable prompt history
[mcp] add type assertion guards
body:
In McpTool.Info(), the code assumes specific shapes for tool.InputSchema during casting.  We add guards to prevent panics.

- [X] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

I was reviewing the latest releases and saw that there was an upgrade from `mcp-go` to the `modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`.  As I've used the latter `go-mcp`, I was familiar with updating from breaking change from a type-assertive API to its later "safe" API.   I saw the new one uses naked type assertions.   I thought that was a bad idea, and spent time looking at flow to see that maybe it was safe.   But component-level it's not clear.

I used crush to do this along with ChatGPT-5 with some hand-edits.   The AI noticed another concern of deeper type-casting of `[]any` to `[]string`.   I asked it if it was sure -- it does make sense in a general case, I think.    Anyway, here's the conversation.

Thanks for `crush`!  All that was human, the following is my crush session.

----

`EW: look at the code in mcp-tools.go   i am concerned that there needs to be type assertions`

Thanks — I reviewed internal/llm/agent/mcp-tools.go with a focus on places where dynamic types are used and where type assertions could fail or be unsafe.

Key findings and fixes needed:

- In McpTool.Info(), the code assumes specific shapes for tool.InputSchema:
  - input := b.tool.InputSchema.(map[string]any)
  - required, _ := input["required"].([]string)
  - properties, _ := input["properties"].(map[string]any)
- The MCP Tool input schema is JSON Schema-like, and after JSON unmarshalling, arrays typically come through as []any, not []string. This makes required, _ := input["required"].([]string) always fail, silently yielding an empty required slice. Also, input itself may not always be a map[string]any, and properties might be absent or of a different type.
- In runTool(), the iteration over result.Content is guarded properly with a type assertion to *mcp.TextContent and a safe fallback, which is fine.

What I will change:

- Make Info() robust by:
  - Safely asserting b.tool.InputSchema to map[string]any, falling back to empty fields if not.
  - Converting required from []any to []string if present and properly typed.
  - Passing through properties only if it’s a map[string]any; otherwise default to nil or empty map.

Plan:

- Update Info() to handle type assertions defensively with conversions.
- Run diagnostics to ensure no type errors.

Now I will implement the changes to McpTool.Info() accordingly and then run diagnostics.

----

I updated McpTool.Info() to perform safe type assertions and conversions for the MCP tool’s InputSchema:

• Guarded the map[string]any assertion on InputSchema.
• Properly handle required when it is []any (most common after JSON unmarshal) by converting elements to []string;
also accept []string directly.
• Only set Parameters when properties is a map[string]any; otherwise leave nil.

Project diagnostics show no new issues.

----

`EW: can you double-check the thinking about needing to check both []any and []string`

Short answer: yes, we should check both. Here’s why:

• The MCP Tool input schema ultimately comes from JSON. Go’s encoding/json unmarshals JSON arrays into []any by
default when the target type is interface{}.
• In practice, b.tool.InputSchema is interface{}, and tool schemas flow through JSON unmarshalling. Therefore,
required is most commonly []any with string elements.
• However, depending on upstream types (e.g., if the SDK or another layer already typed the field as []string, or
if a custom unmarshal occurs), required may already be []string.
• To be robust across both cases, we need to:
• Prefer handling []any and convert elements to []string.
• Also accept []string directly in case the type is already specific.


This dual check prevents silently dropping required keys (which was happening before with only []string) and
avoids panics or incorrect assumptions across different providers/SDK versions.

fix(mcp): improve STDIO error handling
body:
If a stdio mcp prints an error in non-json format, it'll fail to parse, and the cli will then close it, causing the EOF error.

so, if we got an EOF err, and the transport is STDIO, we try to exec it again with a timeout and collect the output so we can add details to the error.

this happens particularly when starting things with npx, e.g. if node can't be found or some other error like that.

refs https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/issues/1234

### Description

Hi team!

When pasting a long block of text into Crush (for example, when feeding a long code snippet or JSON), the entire content is printed in the prompt buffer, which makes the input view cluttered and noisy.

title: Prompt Re-Processing - Performance regression starting with v0.11.0

title: Hosted config schema (charm.land/crush.json) is outdated
body: ## Problem The `config.json` schema at https://charm.land/crush.json (referenced with ```"$schema": "https://charm.land/crush.json"```, as per [README.md](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/main/README.md#attribution-settings)) is far behind [schema.json](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/main/schema.json) on `main`. ### Notable differences - Missing top-level fields: `default_provider`, `disable_provider_auto_update` - `ProviderConfig`: uses `disable` instead of `disabled`; missing newer provider types (`mistral`, `ollama`, etc) - `Model`: missing `supports_tools` and `attribution` - `ProviderConfig` + `Model`: no `attribution` block (added for provenance / licensing) - `Permissions`: missing `denied_tools`, `allow_network`, `allow_shell` - `Options`: lacks newer runtime/telemetry options - `MCPConfig`: missing `retry_attempts`, `retry_delay`, and renames `type` → `transport` - `LSPConfig`: uses `enabled` instead of `disabled`, no `root_uri` - `TUIOptions`: missing `theme` and `show_usage_tips` - `additionalProperties`: several sections now allow `true`, but the old version still enforces `false` ## Impact Configs validated against the hosted schema fail or warn when using current features, even though they're valid. This affects everyone with a `crush.json` file somewhere. Fixing this makes it easier for users (and LLMs!) to configure Crush, as they will no longer have to search through the source code (or GitHub Issues) to discover what can be configured. ## Solution - [x] Configure https://charm.land/crush.json to always mirror the latest [schema.json](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/main/schema.json) from `main` - [ ] Pre-`v1.0.0` bonus: version it, like `https://charm.land/crush/0.11/schema.json` (see [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/guides/configure-biome/#configuration-file-structure)) This way, future schema changes are automatically reflected and `config.json` files will validate consistently. 💘 ### Version v0.11.2 (Homebrew) ### Environment macOS, Windsurf

title: feat: add persistent command history with arrow key navigation
body:
## Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive command history persistence system that enables users to navigate through previously entered commands using arrow keys. The implementation provides a familiar shell-like experience with session-scoped history storage and intelligent navigation.

## Key Features

### 🗄️ Database Integration
- **New `command_history` table** with optimized schema
  - Indexed on `session_id` and `created_at` for fast queries
  - Foreign key constraints ensure referential integrity
  - Automatic timestamp management via SQLite triggers
- **Type-safe queries** generated using sqlc for compile-time safety
- **Migration support** for seamless rollout to existing installations

### 🔧 Service Layer
- **CommandHistory Service** implementing clean architecture patterns
  - Add commands with automatic whitespace trimming
  - List commands by session with configurable limits
  - Delete session history when needed
- **Automatic history management**
  - Maximum 1000 commands per session
  - Oldest entries removed automatically when limit exceeded
  - FIFO cleanup strategy prevents unbounded database growth
- **PubSub integration** for real-time event notifications
  - Created events when commands are added
  - Deleted events when history is cleared

### ⌨️ UI Integration
- **Arrow key navigation** in the chat editor
  - `↑` (Up): Navigate to previous commands (newer → older)
  - `↓` (Down): Navigate to next commands (older → newer)
- **Smart history mode**
  - Preserves current input when entering history mode
  - Returns to saved input when navigating past the end
  - Cursor automatically moves to end of line after navigation
- **Session lifecycle management**
  - Loads history asynchronously when session is set
  - Clears history state on session change
  - Persists commands after each send operation

## Implementation Details

This implementation follows industry best practices for CLI history management:

1. **Session Isolation**: Each session maintains its own command history, preventing cross-contamination between different conversations

2. **Efficient Storage**: Commands are stored with timestamps and proper indexing for fast retrieval, with automatic cleanup to prevent unbounded growth

3. **Crash-Safe Design**: All database operations use proper transactions and context timeouts for reliability

4. **Intuitive UX**: Navigation behavior matches standard shell patterns (bash/zsh), making it immediately familiar to CLI users

## Database Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE command_history (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    command TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES sessions (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE INDEX idx_command_history_session_id ON command_history(session_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_command_history_created_at ON command_history(created_at);
```

## Testing

Comprehensive unit tests cover:
- ✅ History navigation in both directions
- ✅ Boundary condition handling (beginning/end of history)
- ✅ Input preservation when entering history mode
- ✅ Empty command filtering
- ✅ Session reset behavior

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a pure additive feature with backward compatibility maintained.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify database migration runs correctly on fresh installs
- [ ] Verify migration runs correctly on existing installations
- [ ] Test command persistence after sending messages
- [ ] Test history navigation with ↑/↓ keys
- [ ] Verify session isolation (different sessions have different history)
- [ ] Test history size limits and automatic cleanup
- [ ] Verify no impact on existing functionality
- [ ] Test history behavior across app restarts

## How It Works

1. **When a user sends a command**: The editor component calls the CommandHistory service to persist the command to the database
2. **When a user presses ↑**: The editor navigates backward through the history array, loading previous commands
3. **When a user presses ↓**: The editor navigates forward, eventually returning to the saved current input
4. **When history reaches limit**: The service automatically removes the oldest entries to make room for new ones
5. **When switching sessions**: The editor loads the appropriate history for the new session

## Files Changed

- `internal/app/app.go`: Wire CommandHistory service into App
- `internal/commandhistory/service.go`: Service implementation (new)
- `internal/db/command_history.sql.go`: Generated sqlc code (new)
- `internal/db/db.go`: Database initialization with new queries
- `internal/db/migrations/20251018000000_add_command_history.sql`: Schema migration (new)
- `internal/db/models.go`: CommandHistory model and params
- `internal/db/querier.go`: Extended Querier interface
- `internal/db/sql/command_history.sql`: SQL query definitions (new)
- `internal/tui/components/chat/editor/editor.go`: History navigation logic
- `internal/tui/components/chat/editor/history_test.go`: Unit tests (new)
- `internal/tui/components/chat/editor/keys.go`: Key binding definitions

## References

- Follows best practices outlined in [Eli Bendersky's guide on persistent shell history](https://eli.thegreenplace.net/2013/06/11/keeping-persistent-history-in-bash)
- Inspired by standard shell history implementations (bash, zsh)
- Implements session-scoped history similar to PR #1254

title: Custom OpenAI endpoint not sending max_tokens parameter
body:
### Description

### Description
When using Crush with a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Synthetic.new), the API request fails with an error indicating that `max_tokens` is not being sent or is being set to 0.

**Configuration**

```
{
  "$schema": "https://charm.land/crush.json",
  "providers": {
    "synthetic": {
      "id": "synthetic",
      "name": "Synthetic Llama 405B",
      "base_url": "https://api.synthetic.new/openai/v1",
      "type": "openai",
      "api_key": "syn_***",
      "models": [
        {
          "id": "hf:meta-llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct",
          "name": "Llama 3.1 405B Instruct"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Error:**

```
POST "https://api.synthetic.new/openai/v1/chat/completions": 400 Bad Request "Error from inference backend: 400 You requested a length 0 completion, but you did not set the 'echo' parameter. That means that we will return no data to you. (HINT: set 'echo' to true in order for the API to echo back the prompt to you.)"
```

**Expected behavior:**

Crush should send a valid `max_tokens` parameter with chat completion requests.

**Works with the following curl:**
```
curl https://api.synthetic.new/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hf:meta-llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
    "max_tokens": 100
  }'
```

This curl command works perfectly, suggesting the issue is with how Crush constructs requests for custom OpenAI endpoints.

### Version

0.11.2

### Environment

macOS 15.6.1 (24G90)

title: Whole "crush" package is in "internal" folder so cannot be imported
body:
One of our teams is doing an eval, of all of the AI coding tools; to figure out why some models are broken in certain tools (bug hunting/eval/tool usage problems). And we need to import the tool libraries for tool replay as part of regression testing.

However, the crush application is in directory called "internal" so none of the libraries inside of crush can be imported. And it makes it difficult to wrap the entry point and control programmatically.

I would suggest, renaming folder from "internal" and allowing imports and design repo, for automatic testing by import/wrap later.

There is bug in opencode/crush with some open router providers and the tool calling, that is impacting open source model and doesnt occur in LLVM and its very very difficult to figure out what is going on, unless there is programmatic hook or tool replay is exported.

I think some inference providers may be rolling their own or there is something weird going on and it only occurs when forwarded to some inference provider under some conditions; definitely stochastic. And the bug depends on specific implementations of tools by the coding tool.

I think keeping the code in "internal" and stopping import from external applications is bad in the long term. 

It would help to have some type of headless mode and have some support for importing and controlling crush programmatically. And that is hindered by use of "internal" to stop external imports.

title: fix: always fetch providers live and not in background
body:
We have this behavior that, if the cache is newer than 24 hours, we skip updating it live and do it in background instead. This is done to supposedly make boot a little bit quickier.

Problem is that potential changes weren't being reflected until Crush is restarted.

This PR essentially make updates always happen live so provider updates are seen immediately.

Keep in mind that we're still saving a cache on `providers.json` that is useful on future
runs if Crush is ran with `CRUSH_DISABLE_PROVIDER_AUTO_UPDATE=1`.

title: Crush integrated AI assistant for documentation/configuration/general help
body:
### Description

Hi, 
Getting started with crush. But I see a **spot that could need immediate attention for helping getting new users started**.

**That would be a integrated crush assistant.**
What I mean is to use the the LLM interact with crush to help the user for configuration/documentation/git issues.

Coming from aider, I got used to /cmd so perhaps starting the conversation with `crush` or `Crush` **_could trigger a specific mode that is not interacting with the current code/project but with crush itself_** ? Why not have a way to ask for help on using crush ? I don't like going to a menu, but I would personally remap `./` for files and keep `/` for running commands.

Watching some crush video : 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3crlgrd86r0
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MXOP4WELkCc

There are some nice feedback.
One of them is to use natural language to ask questions about crush or the mcp servers connected.

So I suppose we could have a few markdown files and some sort of quick RAG to pull context to the llm and ask a question. It could even pull up-to date info from git/crush website.

Now this crush interface should : 
- **Provide answers on topics found in crush documentation**
- Search github issues for related issues or feature requests similar to what is asked
  - Help prepare a bug issue or feature request (writing template, asking questions to make it more comprehensive and specific)
- **help modify crush configurations files**
  - ex.: `crush add edit to allowed tools`
  - ex.: `crush what mcp would help lower my token usage or enhance my productivity? How can I install them ?`
  - ex: `crush add local provider qwen a3b at localhost:8111`
      - will try to generate config, if info missing ask user or propose choices (llamacpp, ollama?) with selection choices and editable boxes as TUI.... Then try testing the configuration : Got error 503, listing models, model name provided by user is wrong, provide list of available models at that address....
- help debug session
  - ex: `crush I tried to add _function_ to my code but it changed a bunch of things, help me revert the changes to when _other_function_ was added`
    - will use git commands to search commits and provide a list of commits with diffs (aka gitui) and recommend the best commit, then offer the command to revert and ask user what commit he wants to revert to.
- general help : `crush compress local folder to bz2 and exclude .git and .gitignore files and save it to /mnt/usb/project_bk.tar.bz2`

Run specialized templates/workflow/plugin for crush (ambitious wish) 
   - crush create `crush plugin` for creating a project architect that will go back and forth with the user asking him questions about the desired project, proposing different implementation types, generating a comprehensive plan for implementation, chunking the plan in actionable tasks, tracking tasks and progress, support adding TODO to future version without immediate implementation, support git issues for bugs and merge for code fix. Use TUI elements to interact with the user in a interactive way ...
   - 
- EDIT: but I would go further and hope something like this is possible : `crush this large codebase has bugs, make a plan to debug it with available models, optimize using small models for simple tool call, use model XXX for code review, model YYY to reorder the issues in the code review and generate a plan to tackle them by priority. Use model XXX to review the plan and ask it for enhancement.` Working... `crush do XX first and execute the plan` 
 
EDIT: for it to function well, crush documentation should be kept to date and have additional sections : 
- FAQ
   -> crush should ask user, if a question is not answered correctly, if he wants to post-it online : 
     have a new git repository `(crush-qa)` for managing questions as issues to not flood crush development bugs with questions. This repository could hold all documentation in .md related to crush, management of it should be semi-agentic and as soon as a issue is marked as closed, generate Q-A -> classify it, check where it should go, append it to the .md.
    - use a index.md with each config section containing a short summary and links to subsection to help manage context
- Config edits rules and documentation as .md describing every option available for configuration with a .json.
    - Automate generating those from  source code with agents.
- Plugin should have separate docs
- MCP : keep a list of mcp servers that works well with crush, with a description of default commands and general description/user review, installation commands for crush to make it run locally and available to the user.
- Roadmap, release info, current bugs should also have their .md so user can check like : `crush what's new since version X?` or `crush I want to do a _feature_ can it be done ?` -> no, that feature is planned for version XXX.

EDIT: 
Crush should have access to some sort of MCP that can interact with the user using TUI, like `text box` `check box` `string` etc. I use AI to preprocess my prompts and enhance it, asking it for suggestions, enhancements or clarification questions. I would like to be provided with a list of checkbox to accept such suggestions or even edit it manually or by an other AI call (only a part of the suggestions) then have an other call to finalize the prompt and asking for `RUN`, `MANUAL_EDIT`, `AI_EDIT`, `SAVE`, `CANCEL`.  Think of it like some sort of `scratch pad` (emacs?) with AI edit capabilities, that should only work on the prompts and have access to the project but no modification access. That way you could ask crush in scratch mode to generate a list of filenames/issues/function_names/etc and append that to the scratch message.

Thanks,
I have other suggestions, but this is the most impactful.
Keep up the good work.

title: Bug: `crush run` fails to execute tool calls (file writing) while interactive mode works
body:
### Description

# Bug: `crush run` fails to execute tool calls (file writing) while interactive mode works

## Description

When using `crush run` with models that support tool calling (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro), the agent fails to write files or execute any tool calls. The same prompt works perfectly in interactive mode.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Crush with a tool-calling capable model (e.g., GPT-5 or Gemini 2.5 Pro)
2. Run a simple file writing task in interactive mode:
   ```bash
   crush
   # Then type: "Write a joke and save it to joke.txt"
   ```
   **Result**: ✅ File is created successfully

3. Run the same task using `crush run`:
   ```bash
   crush run -q "Write a joke and save it to joke.txt"
   ```
   **Result**: ❌ File is NOT created, no tool calls are executed

## Expected Behavior

`crush run` should execute tool calls (like file writing) just as interactive mode does.

## Actual Behavior

In `crush run` mode, the agent appears to run without any tools available, so it cannot write files or execute any other tool operations.

## Root Cause

I've traced through the code and found a **race condition** in the agent initialization:

### The Problem

In `internal/agent/coordinator.go`, the `buildAgent()` method (lines 303-310) initializes tools **asynchronously** in a goroutine:

```go
result := NewSessionAgent(SessionAgentOptions{
    large,
    small,
    largeProviderCfg.SystemPromptPrefix,
    systemPrompt,
    c.cfg.Options.DisableAutoSummarize,
    c.permissions.SkipRequests(),
    c.sessions,
    c.messages,
    nil,  // <-- Tools are nil here
})
go func() {
    tools, err := c.buildTools(ctx, agent)
    if err != nil {
        slog.Error("could not init agent tools", "err", err)
        return
    }
    result.SetTools(tools)  // <-- Tools set asynchronously
}()
return result, nil  // <-- Agent returned immediately
```

The agent is **returned immediately** before the goroutine completes, meaning `a.tools` is still `nil` when the agent is first used.

In `internal/agent/agent.go`, the `Run()` method (lines 133-142) creates the Fantasy agent with whatever tools are available at that moment:

```go
if len(a.tools) > 0 {
    a.tools[len(a.tools)-1].SetProviderOptions(a.getCacheControlOptions())
}

agent := fantasy.NewAgent(
    a.largeModel.Model,
    fantasy.WithSystemPrompt(a.systemPrompt),
    fantasy.WithTools(a.tools...),  // <-- If tools aren't loaded yet, this is empty
)
```

### Why Interactive Mode Works

In interactive mode, there's a natural delay between agent initialization and the first user prompt (UI rendering, user typing, etc.). This gives the goroutine enough time to complete and set the tools before the first `Run()` call.

### Why `crush run` Fails

In `crush run` mode, the prompt is executed **immediately** after agent creation in `internal/app/app.go:154`:

```go
result, err := app.AgentCoordinator.Run(ctx, sess.ID, prompt)
```

This happens before the async `SetTools()` completes, so the agent runs with zero tools.

## Suggested Fix

Remove the asynchronous goroutine and make tool initialization synchronous:

```go
result := NewSessionAgent(SessionAgentOptions{
    large,
    small,
    largeProviderCfg.SystemPromptPrefix,
    systemPrompt,
    c.cfg.Options.DisableAutoSummarize,
    c.permissions.SkipRequests(),
    c.sessions,
    c.messages,
    nil,
})

tools, err := c.buildTools(ctx, agent)
if err != nil {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("could not init agent tools: %w", err)
}
result.SetTools(tools)

return result, nil
```

Alternatively, if async initialization is desired for performance reasons, add a synchronization mechanism to ensure tools are loaded before the agent can be used.

## Environment

- **Version**: v0.13.3 (latest as of 2025-10-28)
- **OS**: Tested on Linux
- **Models tested**: GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro

## Additional Context

This appears to be related to the recent refactoring work (commit `14f2f9c7` and the Fantasy library integration). The async tool initialization was likely added for performance optimization in interactive mode but creates a race condition for non-interactive usage.


### Version

v0.13.3

### Environment

linux (fedora), ghostty

title: Fix race condition in tool initialization for non-interactive mode
body:
This commit fixes a race condition where 'crush run' would execute before tools were fully initialized, causing tool calls (like file writing) to fail in non-interactive mode while working in interactive mode.

The fix uses a sync.WaitGroup to coordinate tool initialization:
- Tools are still loaded asynchronously in a goroutine (preserving performance benefits for interactive mode)
- The Run() method now waits for tools to be ready before proceeding
- Zero performance impact on interactive mode (UI renders immediately)
- Ensures 'crush run' blocks until tools are available

This maintains the async optimization for interactive mode while ensuring correctness for non-interactive usage.

Fixes issue where models with tool calling support (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) could not execute tool operations in 'crush run' mode.

title: fix(tui): disable progress bar for iterm2 and over ssh
body:
This will conditionally query the terminal for its version and name on startup. If the program is run locally or the TERM_PROGRAM variable is set to a non-Apple terminal, Crush will query for the terminal version. Otherwise, if the terminal is known to support XTVERSION, it will also query for the version even if it was over SSH.

The problem is that Apple Terminal does not support XTVERSION, and when we query for XTVERSION, it render some jargon that might break the UI.

Once we get a response, we send progress-bar update messages only if the terminal is _not_ iTerm2 since it doesn't support that yet.

Fixes: https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/issues/1326

fix: rethink global config path on windows: use `$HOME/.config`
body:
* Fixes #1347

We made a mistake when it comes to the global config path on Windows. On macOS and Linux we use two different paths for data and config: `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. On Windows though, we were using the same path for both data and config: `LOCALAPPDATA`. This caused confusion and means the user has no separate dir to store config separate of data.

In theory we could consider something as `APPDATA`, but honestly, I propose that we just use `$HOME/.config`. It's easier to find and consistent with how other tools work. Git and other terminal tools also use `$HOME/.config`, so users are used to it.

This is not a breaking change because the old path will still load, so existing setting will load as expected.

title: fix(config): correctly check cache staleness before fetching providers
body:
Previously, loadProviders was ignoring the 'stale' return value from isCacheStale(), causing unnecessary fetches from Catwalk even when cache was fresh. This resulted in frequent network requests for the same provider data.

Fixes:
- Capture both 'stale' and 'exists' return values from isCacheStale()
- Only fetch from Catwalk when cache doesn't exist OR is stale (>24h)
- Use cached providers when cache exists and is fresh

Updates `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk's releases.

v1.1.0

This release introduces a few new features, and includes improvements and bug fixes for the streamable transport. Notably, the default behavior of the streamable server transport is changed to disable streams resumption (see #580).

Behavior Changes

Stream resumption disabled by default. In the StreamableServerTransport, the default value of nil for the EventStore field now disables stream resumption, rather than defaulting to use an in-memory event store. Resumption is not desirable in many cases, particularly for servers that must serve a large number of users and/or streams.

If you want to enable resumption, set StreamableHTTPOptions.EventStore.

In general, we will avoid changing behaviors that may be relied upon by users, but in this case the old default was deemed to be an oversight/bug, and fixing it now will benefit future users.

API Additions

  • IOTransport is a new general-purpose transport constructed from an io.ReadCloser and io.WriteCloser (#444 ).
  • ServerOptions.Logger and StreamableHTTPOptions.Logger enable server-side logging (#170).
  • StreamableHTTPOptions.EventStore enables stream resumption (#587).
  • StreamableHTTPOptions.SessionTimeout adds a timeout which, when set, causes idle sessions to be automatically closed (#499).

Experimental client-side oauth support

The auth package now includes experimental APIs when build with the mcp_go_client_oauth build tag. See auth/client.go for more details. These APIs may change before their official release.
