title: refactor: terminal capability handling
body:
This streamlines the handling of terminal capabilities by introducing a dedicated Capabilities struct within the common package. This struct centralizes the management of terminal features such as color profiles, dimensions, and graphics support.

It provides a query command to fetch terminal capabilities and methods to update and check support for specific features. This refactor enhances code clarity and maintainability by encapsulating capability-related logic in a single location.

We only query for capabilities on program startup specifically after we get the program's environment variables. We need the environment variables to determine what capabilities to query for since some terminals like Apple Terminal bleeds characters when we query for certain capabilities.

Honorable mention: https://github.com/dankamongmen/notcurses/blob/c951e0c3ebb4aa26cdaaa8e4a7bbf7d9e7d68cf3/src/lib/termdesc.c#L1114

## Summary

Addresses context overflow from large tool outputs by:

- **Default tail behavior**: Bash tool now shows last 100 lines by default instead of truncating from middle
- **Full output caching**: Stores complete output in a per-session cache (30 min retention)
- **Exploration tools**: Three new tools for agents to dig into large outputs:
  - `output_head` - View first N lines with pagination
  - `output_tail` - View last N lines with pagination
  - `output_grep` - Search with regex, returns matching line numbers

1. When bash (or other tools) produces large output, only last 100 lines shown to agent
2. Response includes `tool_call_id` and truncation info: `[Showing last 100 of 5432 lines. Use output_head/output_tail/output_grep with tool_call_id="xyz" to explore full output]`

## Summary

Adds Anthropic OAuth device flow authentication, allowing users to authenticate with their Anthropic account instead of using API keys directly.

## Features

### 1. OAuth Device Flow (`internal/oauth/anthropic/`)

Implements the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant:
- Device code request to Anthropic's authorization server
- Polling for token completion
- Token storage and refresh handling

### 2. Tool Name Remapping (`internal/agent/oauth_tools.go`)

When using OAuth tokens, Anthropic's API uses different tool names (e.g., `computer` instead of `bash`). This adds automatic bidirectional remapping:
- Outbound: Convert crush tool names → Anthropic OAuth tool names
- Inbound: Convert Anthropic OAuth tool names → crush tool names

### 3. TUI OAuth Dialog (`internal/ui/dialog/oauth_anthropic.go`)

New dialog for the classic TUI that guides users through OAuth:
- Displays device code and verification URL
- Shows QR code for mobile scanning
- Handles polling and success/error states

### 4. New TUI OAuth Modal (`internal/tui/components/dialogs/anthropic/`)

Fancy modal for the new TUI with:
- Animated device flow UI
- QR code display
- Progress indicators

### 5. Stealth Mode

When authenticated via OAuth, the agent operates in "stealth mode":
- Uses Anthropic's Claude Code compatible endpoints
- Tool names are automatically remapped
- Seamless integration with existing workflows

## Files Changed

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `internal/oauth/anthropic/oauth.go` | OAuth device flow implementation |

title: Fix: "This version of Antigravity is no longer supported" error
body:
## Problem

When using OpenCode/Crush with Antigravity plugin, users may encounter this error:
```
This version of Antigravity is no longer supported
```

## Root Cause

The `userAgent` version in `~/.config/opencode/antigravity-accounts.json` is outdated. Antigravity now requires **version 1.15.8** (released on January 24, 2026).

## Solution

**Step 1: Backup your accounts file**
```bash
cp ~/.config/opencode/antigravity-accounts.json ~/.config/opencode/antigravity-accounts.json.backup
```

**Step 2: Update all User-Agent versions to 1.15.8**
```bash
sed -i -E 's/"antigravity\/1\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/"antigravity\/1.15.8/g' ~/.config/opencode/antigravity-accounts.json
```

**Step 3: Clear OpenCode cache**
```bash
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode
```

**Step 4: Kill and restart OpenCode**
```bash
pkill -9 opencode
opencode run "test" --model=google/antigravity-gemini-3-flash
```

## Verification

Check that all accounts now show the updated version:
```bash
cat ~/.config/opencode/antigravity-accounts.json | jq '.accounts[].fingerprint.userAgent'
```

All accounts should now show `"antigravity/1.15.8"` with their respective platform suffixes.

## Environment

- OS: Linux (Ubuntu)
- OpenCode version: 1.1.26
- Plugin: `opencode-antigravity-auth@latest`

---

**Note:** This issue was originally encountered with OpenCode but applies to Crush as well since it's the continuation of the project.

This solution has been tested and confirmed working on 2026-01-30.

title: fix: Add HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY environment variable support to fetch tools
body:
## Summary

- Fixes fetch tools to respect standard HTTP proxy environment variables
- Replaces custom `http.Transport` with cloned `http.DefaultTransport` 
- Maintains all existing connection pool settings and timeouts
- Enables Crush to work in corporate/enterprise environments behind proxies

## Problem

The fetch-related tools were creating custom `http.Transport` instances without proxy support, causing them to ignore standard environment variables:
- `HTTP_PROXY` / `http_proxy`
- `HTTPS_PROXY` / `https_proxy` 
- `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy`

This made Crush unusable in many enterprise environments that require HTTP proxies.

## Solution

Changed all HTTP client creation from:
```go
client = &http.Client{
	Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
	Transport: &http.Transport{
		MaxIdleConns:        100,
		MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 10,
		IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
	},
}
```
To:
```go
transport := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
transport.MaxIdleConns = 100
transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost = 10
transport.IdleConnTimeout = 90 * time.Second

client = &http.Client{
	Timeout:   30 * time.Second,
	Transport: transport,
}
```

Closes #2060

title: Zed-like saved prompts
body:
### Description

Zed has an amazing feature that no other agent has (including Zed's agent!): inline prompts.

The way it works is super simple and super powerful: in Zed's `Text Thread` feature, you type `/prompt <prompt name>`

```
/prompt MyGreatPrompt
```

It then pastes (under a disclosure triangle) the entire saved prompt, allowing you to edit it as you see fit before submitting it to the LLM.

Crush could also support this in relation to its `^o` feature (which opens an editor).

You'd type something like `/prompt` or `@prompt` and it would read the titles of various prompts saved under `~/.config/crush/prompts`, allowing you to select from one of them.

When you hit `<enter>` it would open the editor with that prompt pasted in. Then you can continue editing to your liking.

This is a great way to save frequently-used prompts.

## How is this different from Skills?

Skills don't allow you to edit them. With Skills you have to tell the agent to use the specific skill, and then it reads the file and that's it. But with saved prompts, you can edit them immediately before submitting them to the AI.

title: Add support for ~/.agents/skills folder
body:
### Description

**Current Behavior:**
Currently, Crush Code Agent exclusively looks for custom skills and tools within the project-specific directory `.crush/skills`. While this is useful for project isolation, it creates silos that prevent skills from being easily shared across different projects or other code agent tools.

**Desired Behavior:**
Crush Code Agent should also load skills from the standardized user-level directory: `~/.agents/skills/`.

**Motivation / Why Standardization Matters:**
The ecosystem of AI code agents is rapidly evolving. To improve interoperability and user experience, there is a growing community consensus towards adopting a universal standard for storing agent configurations and skills.

By supporting `~/.agents/skills`:
1.  **Cross-Tool Compatibility:** Users can write a skill once and have it available across multiple compatible agents, without duplicating files.
2.  **Centralized Management:** It provides a single, clean location for users to manage their high-quality, reusable prompts and tools globally.
3.  **Future-Proofing:** Aligning with the `~/.agents/` standard ensures Crush remains an open and flexible tool within the broader developer ecosystem.

**Suggested Implementation:**
I propose adding a fallback search path or a merged loading strategy:
1.  **Priority:** Check `.crush/skills` first (for project-specific overrides).
2.  **Global Fallback:** If a skill is not found locally, check `~/.agents/skills/`.
3.  **OR:** Merge both directories so that skills in `~/.agents/skills` are always available alongside local ones.

title: LSP auto-discovery over aggressive
body:
### Description

Introduced in https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/pull/1834, crush has the ability to find LSP servers that are installed with root markers in your project that match the config from powernap (from nvim-lspconfig).

This line simply checks if the lsp server's `command` exists in `PATH`
https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/133cb6f9b03d769e5328e5124506e1c6e321c075/internal/app/lsp.go#L89-L93 

The problem is that some LSP servers use a generic runtime/interpreter as the command rather than a unique server executable.
eg.
https://github.com/charmbracelet/x/blob/b72a9a918687c94820f03576ca16835bcf09919c/powernap/pkg/config/lsps.json#L328

So in this case, `tvm_ffi_nagivator` is started even though I don't have it installed simply due to me having python and the root markers matching.

I think this is the case for a number of other servers as well. 
I think these are the worst offenders are...
```json
{
  "alloy_ls": {"command": "alloy", "args": ["lsp"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["alloy"]},
  "bright_script": {"command": "bsc", "args": ["--lsp", "--stdio"], "root_markers": ["makefile", "Makefile", ".git"], "filetypes": ["brs"]},
  "dafny": {"command": "dafny", "args": ["server"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["dfy", "dafny"]},
  "esbonio": {"command": "python3", "args": ["-m", "esbonio"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["rst"]},
  "futhark_lsp": {"command": "futhark", "args": ["lsp"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["futhark", "fut"]},
  "glasgow": {"command": "glasgow", "args": [], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["wgsl"]},
  "koka": {"command": "koka", "args": ["--language-server", "--lsstdio"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["koka"]},
  "muon": {"command": "muon", "args": ["analyze", "lsp"], "root_markers": null, "filetypes": ["meson"]},
  "perlls": {"command": "perl", "args": ["-MPerl::LanguageServer", "-e", "Perl::LanguageServer::run", "--", "--port 13603", "--nostdio 0"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["perl"]},
  "r_language_server": {"command": "R", "args": ["--no-echo", "-e", "languageserver::run()"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["r", "rmd", "quarto"]},
  "racket_langserver": {"command": "racket", "args": ["--lib", "racket-langserver"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["racket", "scheme"]},
  "tilt_ls": {"command": "tilt", "args": ["lsp", "start"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["tiltfile"]},
  "turtle_ls": {"command": "node", "args": ["--stdio"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["turtle", "ttl"]},
  "tvm_ffi_navigator": {"command": "python", "args": ["-m", "ffi_navigator.langserver"], "root_markers": ["pyproject.toml", ".git"], "filetypes": ["python", "cpp"]},
  "uiua": {"command": "uiua", "args": ["lsp"], "root_markers": ["main.ua", ".fmt.ua", ".git"], "filetypes": ["uiua"]},
  "vespa_ls": {"command": "java", "args": ["-jar", "vespa-language-server.jar"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["sd", "profile", "yql"]},
  "ziggy": {"command": "ziggy", "args": ["lsp"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["ziggy"]},
  "ziggy_schema": {"command": "ziggy", "args": ["lsp", "--schema"], "root_markers": [".git"], "filetypes": ["ziggy_schema"]}
}
```

But many of these won't be an issue currently since it looks like `.git` is ignored as `root_markers` currently.
https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/133cb6f9b03d769e5328e5124506e1c6e321c075/internal/lsp/client.go#L610

I'm not sure if this is a bug or intended.
With how many lsp servers are configured to use `.git` as a root marker and `.git` alone, I feel like ignoring it is a separate bug.
But if it's not ignored, any project where you have `.git` and you also happen to have `perl` installed, crush is going to try to start `perlls` no?

I'm not sure what the correct approach to handling this would be. Maybe removing auto-discovery for some of the worst offenders on this list?

Another improvement could be to lazily start the lsp servers. So only start `perlls` (assuming root markers and command exists) when a perl file is viewed via the `view` tool.
This won't solve the issue with `tvm-ffi-navigator` though. 


### Repro instructions
1. `cd /tmp && mkdir crush-test && cd crush-test`
2. `touch pyproject.toml`
3. have `python` in path but NOT `pip install --user ffi-navigator`
4. `crush`
5. observe `● tvm_ffi_navigator error: failed to initia…`

## Summary

Adds a configurable `timeout` field to `LSPConfig` to allow users to customize the initialization timeout for LSP servers.

## Motivation

Some LSP servers, particularly those built on the JVM like kotlin-language-server, can take longer than the default 30 seconds to initialize. This causes "context deadline exceeded" errors and prevents the LSP from working properly.

## Changes

- Added `Timeout int` field to `LSPConfig` struct with JSON schema validation
- Modified LSP initialization logic to use the configured timeout value
- Falls back to 30 seconds if not specified
- Updated schema.json with the new field definition

## Usage Example

```json
{
  "lsp": {
    "kotlin": {
      "command": "kotlin-language-server",
      "args": [],
      "filetypes": ["kt", "kts"],
      "root_markers": ["build.gradle.kts"],
      "timeout": 60
    }
  }
}
```

Fixes #1865

```go
        ID:           AgentCoder,  // ✓ Correct
        Name:         "Coder",
        Description:  "An agent that helps with executing coding tasks.",
        Model:        SelectedModelTypeLarge,
        ContextPaths: c.Options.ContextPaths,
        AllowedTools: allowedTools,
    },
    
    AgentTask: {
        ID:           AgentCoder,  // ❌ BUG: Should be AgentTask, not AgentCoder
        Name:         "Task",
        Description:  "An agent that helps with searching for context and finding implementation details.",
        Model:        SelectedModelTypeLarge,
        ContextPaths: c.Options.ContextPaths,
        AllowedTools: resolveReadOnlyTools(allowedTools),
        AllowedMCP:   map[string][]string{},
    },
}
```

### Impact
This bug causes:
1. **Agent Misidentification**: Code that accesses `cfg.Agents[config.AgentTask]` may receive configuration intended for the Coder agent or vice versa
2. **Tool Access Violations**: The Task agent should have restricted tool access (read-only tools only), but with the wrong ID, this restriction can be bypassed or conflated
3. **MCP/LSP Misconfiguration**: The Task agent explicitly disables MCPs (`AllowedMCP: map[string][]string{}`), but with the duplicate ID, the behavior is unpredictable
4. **Potential Logic Errors**: Any code branch that checks `agentID == config.AgentTask` will fail to match correctly

### Affected Code Paths
The following files reference `config.AgentTask` and could be affected:
- `internal/agent/agent_tool.go:28` — Uses `c.cfg.Agents[config.AgentTask]` to build the task agent

### Reproduction Steps
1. Load the configuration via `config.Load()`
2. Access `cfg.Agents[config.AgentTask]`
3. Check the `ID` field of the returned `Agent` struct
4. **Expected**: `ID` should equal `"task"`
5. **Actual**: `ID` equals `"coder"` (same as `AgentCoder`)

### Suggested Fix
Replace `AgentCoder` with `AgentTask` on line 754:

```go
AgentTask: {
    ID:           AgentTask,  // ✓ Corrected
    Name:         "Task",
    Description:  "An agent that helps with searching for context and finding implementation details.",
    Model:        SelectedModelTypeLarge,
    ContextPaths: c.Options.ContextPaths,
    AllowedTools: resolveReadOnlyTools(allowedTools),
    AllowedMCP:   map[string][]string{},
},
```

### Constants Referenced
- `AgentCoder = "coder"` (line 67)
- `AgentTask = "task"` (line 68)

### Severity
**High** — This is a clear copy-paste error that breaks agent configuration and identification logic. Functional impact depends on how strictly agent IDs are validated throughout the codebase.

title: fix(image): HTTP image loading is completely broken
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

## Problem
The `loadURL` function in `internal/tui/components/image/load.go` was creating an HTTP request but never executing it. The code used `http.NewRequestWithContext()` but failed to call `client.Do()`, causing the response body to always be
`nil` for HTTP URLs. Remote image loading was completely non-functional.

## Root Cause
```go
  // Before (broken):
  var resp *http.Request
  resp, err = http.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), http.MethodGet, url, nil)
  r = resp.Body  // resp.Body is nil - request never executed!
```

## Solution
The fix properly creates, executes, and validates HTTP requests:

1. Creates request with  http.NewRequestWithContext()
2. Executes request using  http.DefaultClient.Do()
3. Validates HTTP status code (only accepts 2xx responses)
4. Closes response body on error status codes
5. Returns response body for successful requests

## Impact
•    Remote image loading now works correctly
•    Proper error handling for non-2xx status codes
•    No resource leaks (response bodies closed appropriately)
•    Local file loading continues to work as before

title: fix(app): replace time.After with reusable timer to prevent leak in setupSubscriber
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

The  setupSubscriber  function in  internal/app/app.go  creates a new 2-second timer on every message iteration using
time.After() . When messages are successfully sent to the output channel, these timers are never stopped or drained,
causing them to continue running for their full duration. Under high message throughput (e.g., many LSP diagnostics,
file change events), hundreds or thousands of idle timers accumulate, consuming CPU and memory.

## Impact:
• Memory and CPU leaks during active development with many file changes
• Performance degradation in subscription-heavy scenarios (6 subscriptions: sessions, messages, permissions, history,
mcp, lsp)
• Potential out-of-memory conditions under sustained high load

## Root Cause:

  // Line 274 - creates new timer on every message
  case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
      slog.Debug("Message dropped due to slow consumer", "name", name)

## Fix: 
Replace  time.After()  with a reusable  time.NewTimer()  that's properly stopped, drained, and reset on each
iteration. Added  defer sendTimer.Stop()  for cleanup on goroutine exit.

## Changes:
•  internal/app/app.go:426-470  - Refactored  setupSubscriber  with single reusable timer
•  internal/app/app_test.go  - Added 5 tests including goleak verification
• Added  go.uber.org/goleak v1.3.0  dependency

## Tests:
• All 5 new tests pass, including  TestSetupSubscriber_NoTimerLeak  which uses goleak to verify no goroutine leaks
•  TestSetupSubscriber_DrainAfterDrop  specifically tests the drain-after-drop deadlock scenario

title: chore: update fantasy to v0.7.1
Small model provider never enables Anthropic thinking mode
body:
## Summary
When the small model provider is built we accidentally pass the **large** model configuration into `buildProvider`. That means `isAnthropicThinking` sees the wrong model, so the `anthropic-beta` header that enables thinking mode for Anthropic models is never set for the small provider. As a result, the small model can never enter thinking mode even if its config sets `"think": true` or the provider options enable reasoning.

## Reproduction
1. Configure `models.large` to an OpenAI model (so thinking is disabled there).
2. Configure `models.small` to an Anthropic model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-3.2-sonic`) with `"think": true` (or provider options that request thinking).
3. Start Crush (TUI or `crush run ...`). When the agent coordinator builds the **small** provider (used for summarization/safety), you will never see the `anthropic-beta: interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14` header logged or sent because `buildProvider` is looking at the large model config instead.
4. The small actor therefore never produces any `thinking` output even though the config explicitly asked for it.

## Suggested fix
In `internal/agent/coordinator.go` line ~540 we should be passing `smallModelCfg` into `buildProvider` instead of `largeModelCfg`:

```go
smallProvider, err := c.buildProvider(smallProviderCfg, smallModelCfg, true)
```

That way `isAnthropicThinking` inspects the small-model configuration and adds the header when the small model actually requests thinking.

## Notes
Searched the repo issues for `"anthropic-beta"` and "small model thinking" (e.g. `gh issue list --repo charmbracelet/crush --search "anthropic-beta"`) with no matching bug.

title: feat: implement handoff workflow for context compaction
body:
Discussion: https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/discussions/2140

## Summary

This PR introduces the **Handoff Workflow** - a new context compaction system that preserves important session information across conversation boundaries. When sessions grow too long, instead of losing context through simple blind summarisation, we now generate an information-dense "handoff summary" that the LLM reads first, the past context is archived such that the clear sessions can search with the PastMemorySearch tool.

## Key Changes

### Core Features
- **Past Memory Storage**: Added `past_memory` column to sessions table to store archived conversation context
- **Handoff Summary Generation**: New prompt template (`handoff_summary.md`) creates structured briefings when context windows are exceeded
- **Past Memory Search Tool**: New `past_memory_search` tool allows subagents to query archived context via natural language
- **Subagent-based Search**: The search tool spawns a specialized subagent that can grep and analyze past conversation data

### Database Changes
- Migration: `20260128000000_add_past_memory_to_sessions.sql`
- Updates to `Session` model, queries, and session service

### Agent Changes  
- New `past_memory_tool.go` implementing the search functionality
- `PastMemoryMiniTools` providing grep capabilities on archived context
- Integration with coordinator's tool building

### UI Changes
- New UI actions for handoff workflow in `dialog/actions.go`
- Updated commands and UI model to support the feature

### Templates Added
- `handoff_summary.md` - Prompt for generating dense context briefings
- `past_memory.md` - Template for subagent search prompts

### Removed
- Deprecated `summary.md` template (replaced by handoff approach)

## Best way to use it
1. Completed a unit of work in crush
2. Wanting to do a related task but fear mid-task auto-compaction
3. Trigger handoff manually, explain what is the next task
4. Crush figures out what is needed, bootstraps new context, archives past context if searching becomes necessary.
If the user is unaware of the feature or unwilling to use it, it will be triggered automatically after context is exhausted with a generic request to continue next-task, this allows power users to manage context very surgically.

## Testing
must still be figured out
- [ ] Test migration applies cleanly
- [ ] Test handoff summary generation
- [ ] Test past memory search with various queries
- [ ] Test UI flow for triggering handoff

title: Feature: Sub-agent status sidebar panel
body:
## Summary

Add a sidebar panel that displays active sub-agents and their status, similar to how the TODO list is shown in the sidebar.

## Use Case

When using multi-agent orchestration systems (like OhMyOpenCode's Atlas/Sisyphus pattern), the main agent frequently delegates tasks to sub-agents. Currently, viewing sub-agent status requires:
1. Pressing `Ctrl+X` to open the session switcher
2. Navigating with arrow keys to find the relevant sub-agent session

This workflow interrupts focus and makes it difficult to monitor parallel sub-agent execution at a glance.

## Proposed Solution

A persistent sidebar panel (toggleable, like the TODO panel) showing:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Agent name | The sub-agent identifier (e.g., "sisyphus-1", "explore-2") |
| Task | Brief description of delegated task |
| Status | `running` / `completed` / `failed` |
| Duration | Time elapsed since spawn |

### Mockup

```
┌─ Sub-agents ────────────────┐
│ ● sisyphus-1    [running]   │
│   "Fix auth middleware"     │
│   2m 34s                    │
│                             │
│ ● explore-3     [running]   │
│   "Find error handlers"     │
│   45s                       │
│                             │
│ ✓ librarian-1   [done]      │
│   "Lookup JWT docs"         │
│   1m 12s                    │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

## Related

- #431 - Subagents feature (covers spawning/management, not UI visibility)

## Additional Context

I'm using OhMyOpenCode which adds orchestration capabilities via prompt engineering and MCP tools. The orchestrator delegates to specialized sub-agents, but there's no visibility into their status without manually switching sessions.

Would be happy to contribute to this implementation if there's interest.

```sh
git clone --bare foo/bar
```

then

```sh
git worktree add feat-1
cd feat-1
crush
```

and

```sh
git worktree add feat-2

crush
```

title: fix(mcp): cancel context on MCP session close to prevent leak
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

A `createSession()` function creates a child context in `internal/agent/tools/mcp/init.go`.
A `cancel()` function is correctly called before returning on error paths, it is never called on the success path.

This means every successful MCP connection leaves behind an uncancelled child context
hanging off the parent. The parent context (passed down from the application) can never
fully complete its cancellation tree. When the session is later closed via
`session.Close()`, the underlying transport is torn down, but the context remains
active.

This compounds per configured MCP server. If a user has 5 MCP servers configured,
5 orphaned contexts accumulate. Reconnections via `getOrRenewClient()` create
additional orphaned contexts each time a ping fails and a new session is established.

title: fix(ui): clear image cache when FilePicker closes to prevent unbounded memory growth
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

The global cachedImages map in internal/ui/image/image.go stores decoded image.Image objects keyed by {id, cols, rows}. It has no eviction, no size limit, and no TTL — it only grows. Every unique image file browsed in the FilePicker adds a permanent entry that persists for the entire process lifetime.

Each entry holds a fully decoded RGBA image, which can be several MB of pixel data depending on the source image dimensions.

## Reproduction
1. Open the FilePicker dialog
2. Browse through directories containing many image files (the preview triggers caching)
3. Close the FilePicker
4. Repeat — memory usage only increases, never decreases

## Expected behavior
Cached images should be freed when they are no longer needed. The cache is only used by the FilePicker dialog, so all entries become dead weight the moment the dialog closes.

## Impact
Long-running sessions that frequently use the FilePicker will accumulate unbounded memory from stale image data that will never be accessed again.

title: fix: prevent goroutine orphaning in mcp.Close() and shell.KillAll()
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

mcp.Close() and BackgroundShellManager.KillAll() both use the same pattern: spawn a goroutine to do cleanup, then `select` on a 5-second `time.After`. If the timeout fires first, the function returns but the cleanup goroutine keeps running indefinitely, holding references to MCP sessions or background shells and their resources.                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
## Steps to reproduce
1. Have an MCP server or background shell that is slow to shut down (>5s);
2. Trigger application shutdown (e.g. quit the TUI);
3. The cleanup goroutine is orphaned and leaks until the process exits.

## Fix
Replace the outer goroutine + time.After pattern with context.WithTimeout, matching the established pattern used in 16+ other places in the codebase (e.g. LSPManager.StopAll). Each per-session/per-shell goroutine now races its cleanup against ctx.Done(), so when the deadline fires all goroutines unblock and wg.Wait() returns promptly.

title: fix: clear regex cache on new session to prevent unbounded growth
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

Two global regex caches (searchRegexCache, globRegexCache) in internal/agent/tools/grep.go are backed by plain maps with no eviction. Every unique search pattern and glob pattern compiled during agent tool use is cached permanently. In long-running sessions with varied search patterns, memory grows linearly with unique patterns. Compiled *regexp.Regexp objects can be large depending on complexity.

## Fix
Clear both caches on new session start.

title: fix: safely handle items without Text() interface in completion width (#2154 , #2163)
body:
## Fix: Prevent panic in completions popup
### Problem

When a user types `@afileName` in the editor and the filename doesn't exist (no matching completions), the app panics:

```
panic: interface conversion: list.Item is nil, not interface { Text() string }
```

**Root cause:** In `updateSize()`, the type assertion `item.(interface{ Text() string })` fails when `ItemAt()` returns `nil` for out-of-bounds indices after filtering.
The `updateSize()` function in `completions.go` panics when filtering 
completions. The type assertion `item.(interface{ Text() string })` failed 
when `ItemAt()` returned `nil` or an item that doesn't implement `Text()`.

### Solution
Use safe type assertion with the comma-ok idiom. Skip invalid items with `continue` instead of crashing:
```go
item := c.list.ItemAt(i)
s, ok := item.(interface{ Text() string })
if !ok {
    continue
}
width = max(width, ansi.StringWidth(s.Text()))
```

### Testing
- [x] Manual testing: typed `@`, filtered, navigated - no crash
- [x] `go build` passes
- [x] `go test ./...` passes

title: internal/ui: fix panic in completions width calculation
body:
When the completions list is empty, `VisibleItemIndices` returns `(0, 0)`. The width calculation loop iterates from start to end inclusive, causing it to execute for index 0 even when no items exist.

This results in a panic because `ItemAt(0)` returns nil, which fails the type assertion: interface conversion: interface is `nil`, not `interface { Text() string }`

Fix this by guarding the width calculation loop with a check for len(items) > 0. This ensures we only attempt to access items when the list is non-empty.

- Added TestUpdateSize.

title: Fix: Chinese text not copied correctly to clipboard (#2155)
body:
# Fix: Chinese text not copied correctly to clipboard

## Problem

When selecting and copying text containing Chinese (or other wide) characters, only the English content was copied. The Chinese characters were replaced with spaces.

**Example:**
- Original text: `"你好！我是Crush"`
- Copied text: `"   !    Crush"` (with unwanted spaces)

## Root Cause

Wide characters (like Chinese) occupy 2 terminal columns:
- Position 0: Stores "你" with `Width = 2`
- Position 1: Placeholder cell with `Width = 0` (empty content)

The `line.Set()` function in ultraviolet has a side-effect, when called on a wide character, it first empties all associated cells including placeholders before writing the new value. This converted placeholder cells into space characters.

## Solution I found

In `HighlightBuffer`, replaced `line.Set()` with a direct highlighter call:

```go
// Before (broken):
line.Set(x, highlighter(x, y, cell))

// After (fixed):
highlighter(x, y, cell)
```

Since highlighting only modifies the cell's **style** (not content/width), and the highlighter receives a pointer, calling it directly modifies the cell in place without triggering the corruption side-effect.

## Testing

- [x] `task build` passes
- [x] `task test` passes
- [x] Manual verification: Chinese text can be selected and copied correctly :))

v1.10.0

1.10.0 - 2026-02-04

  • Full Changelog

New Features

  • GetFeatureFlagResult: New method that returns both the flag value and payload in a single call, while properly tracking feature flag usage via $feature_flag_called events.

Deprecations

  • GetFeatureFlagPayload: Deprecated in favor of GetFeatureFlagResult. The new method provides better tracking and a more convenient API.

Migration Guide

// Before (two calls, no event tracking for payload-only):
flag, _ := client.GetFeatureFlag(payload)
payloadStr, _ := client.GetFeatureFlagPayload(payload)

// After (single call, always tracks):
result, err := client.GetFeatureFlagResult(payload)
if err != nil { /* handle */ }
if result.Enabled {
var config MyConfig
result.GetPayloadAs(&config)
}

Note: GetFeatureFlagResult returns nil, error when a flag doesn't exist (rather than a result with Enabled: false). Check for errors to distinguish between a disabled flag and a missing flag:

result, err := client.GetFeatureFlagResult(payload)
if errors.Is(err, posthog.ErrFlagNotFound) {
    // Flag doesn't exist - use default behavior
}
if err != nil {
    // Other error (e.g., network issue)
}
if result.Enabled {
    // Flag exists and is enabled
} else {
    // Flag exists but is disabled
}

title: feat: add configurable auto-background threshold for bash tool
body:
### Summary

- Add `auto_background_after` parameter to allow LLMs to customize the auto-background threshold per command invocation
- Default behavior remains unchanged (60 seconds) when parameter is not provided
- Full test coverage for both default and custom threshold scenarios

### Motivation

The bash tool automatically moves long-running commands to background jobs after a hardcoded 1-minute threshold. This change makes that threshold configurable, allowing the LLM to specify a shorter or longer wait time when it knows a command will take a specific amount of time. For example, a build command expected to take 2 minutes can use `auto_background_after: 150` to avoid premature backgrounding.

#### `crush run` Delegation Workflows

This is particularly important for [`crush run` delegation](https://github.com/portertech/agents-workflow/blob/main/skills/crush-run-delegate/SKILL.md) where:

- **Commands often exceed 60 seconds** for non-trivial delegated tasks
- **Auto-backgrounding breaks the pattern** - the LLM switches to inefficient `job_output` polling

With `auto_background_after`, the LLM can specify a longer threshold (e.g., `auto_background_after: 300`) when invoking `crush run`, ensuring synchronous completion and direct result capture.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `internal/agent/tools/bash.go` | Added `AutoBackgroundAfter` field to `BashParams` and `BashPermissionsParams` structs; updated threshold computation to use custom value when provided |
| `internal/agent/tools/bash.tpl` | Updated documentation to mention the configurable parameter |
| `internal/agent/tools/bash_test.go` | New test file with coverage for default and custom threshold behavior |

### Test Plan

- [x] `go build ./...` succeeds
- [x] `go test ./internal/agent/tools/... -run TestBash` passes
- [x] Verified default threshold (60s) is used when `AutoBackgroundAfter` is 0
- [x] Verified custom threshold is respected when set to a positive value

title: feat(shell): add blocking wait option to job_output tool
body:
### Summary

Adds a `wait` parameter to the `job_output` tool that allows blocking until a background shell completes, with proper context cancellation support.

### Changes

- **`internal/agent/tools/job_output.go`**: Added `Wait bool` parameter to `JobOutputParams`. When `true`, calls `WaitContext(ctx)` before retrieving output, blocking until the shell completes or the request context is cancelled.

- **`internal/agent/tools/job_output.md`**: Updated tool documentation to describe the new `wait` parameter and its behavior.

- **`internal/shell/background.go`**: Added `WaitContext(ctx context.Context) bool` method to `BackgroundShell` that waits for shell completion or context cancellation, returning `true` if the shell completed and `false` if the context was cancelled.

- **`internal/shell/background_test.go`**: Added two test cases:
  - `TestBackgroundShell_WaitContext_Completed` - verifies `true` is returned when shell completes
  - `TestBackgroundShell_WaitContext_Canceled` - verifies `false` is returned when context is cancelled

- **`internal/agent/common_test.go`**: Minor test fix to clear `ContextPaths` to avoid VCR cassette matching issues.

### Motivation

Previously, the `job_output` tool could only poll for output, requiring multiple calls to check if a background process had finished. The new `wait=true` option allows the agent to block until completion, which is useful when:
- The agent needs the final output and exit status
- Polling overhead should be avoided
- The process is expected to complete soon

The context-aware implementation ensures requests don't hang indefinitely—if the request is cancelled, the wait returns early with the current output.

### Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests added for `WaitContext` (both completion and cancellation paths)
- [x] Run `go test ./internal/shell/...`
- [x] Run `go test ./internal/agent/...`
- [x] Verify existing tests pass with `task test`

title: chore(deps): update catwalk to v0.18.0
High CPU usage (~500-600%) when running prompts in large monorepos
body:
I was see crazy high CPU usage (~500-600%) when running prompts in large Typescript monorepo. Tested with a 771,000 file / 73,000 directory repository. Profiles are attached for reference.

### Root Cause Analysis (via pprof)

| Profile | Finding | CPU% |
|---------|---------|------|
| 1 | `regexp.(*Regexp).tryBacktrack` from `sabhiram/go-gitignore` | **80%** |
| 3 | After switching libs: `filepath.Match` + `checkParentIgnores` walking up directories | 34% |
| 4 | After adding combined matchers: `getCombinedMatcher` rebuilding matchers | 16% |
| 5 | After adding `dirPatterns` cache: remaining CPU is syscall overhead (unavoidable filesystem I/O) | ~45% syscalls |

### Solution
1. **Replaced gitignore library**: `github.com/sabhiram/go-gitignore` (compiles each pattern to regex) → `github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/format/gitignore` (native glob matching)
2. **Two-level caching**: `dirPatterns` cache (per-directory patterns) + `combinedMatchers` cache (pre-built matchers for each directory)
3. **O(1) fast-path**: Map lookup for common ignored directories (`node_modules`, `.git`, `__pycache__`, etc.) before any pattern matching
4. **Proper directory handling**: Added `isDir` parameter to correctly match directory-specific patterns (e.g., `backup/`)

### Results
- Gitignore pattern matching dropped from **80% → ~2%** of CPU time
- Remaining CPU is inherent filesystem I/O when walking large directory trees

title: MCP client fails when list resources returns error after session establishment
body: ### Description The Atlassian MCP server implements the MCP spec differently than suggested and returns that it is capable of Resources when it does not implement the List Resources method. This causes crush mcp client to fail during initialization and not allow for any capabilities with this . Crush logs: ``` 2026/02/14 21:28:34 INFO Initializing MCP clients source=github.com/charmbracelet/crush/internal/agent/tools/mcp/init.go:167 2026/02/14 21:28:37 ERRO Error listing resources error="calling \"resources/list\": Method not found" source=github.com/charmbracelet/crush/internal/agent/tools/mcp/init.go:223 ``` However, the resources list call comes as part of the `Normal protocol operations` part of the connection lifecycle. https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle This means it would be considered a request error and not a session error. Furthermore, [MCP spec for resources call](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/resources#error-handling) states: ``` Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Resource not found: -32002 ``` This implies that this is a valid error and should be handled on the client side. To be robust and allow users to continue using the other MCP server capabilities, crush should internally mark `Resources` as unavailable and no longer use them. Code pointer: https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/af86738e0d6edfeb0ae7fb239b8bdabd4c162fca/internal/agent/tools/mcp/resources.go#L83 ### Version master ### Environment OSX

title: feat: add npm distribution with optionalDependencies pattern
body:
## Summary

Adds npm distribution using the **optionalDependencies pattern** (like esbuild, turbo, and opencode) instead of postinstall downloads from GitHub.

This enables `npm install @charmland/crush` to work in **corporate/enterprise environments** where:
- `registry.npmjs.org` is allowed (standard for development)
- `github.com` is blocked (common security policy)

Closes #2230

## Changes

- `scripts/npm-optional-deps/build-npm-packages.sh` - Build script that creates platform packages from goreleaser archives
- `scripts/npm-optional-deps/crush-wrapper.js` - JavaScript wrapper that finds and executes the platform binary
- `scripts/npm-optional-deps/README.md` - Documentation
- `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` - GitHub Actions workflow to automate publishing

## How it works

Instead of:
```
@charmland/crush (postinstall downloads from GitHub)
```

We create:
```
@charmland/crush (thin wrapper)
  └── optionalDependencies:
      ├── @charmland/crush-linux-x64   (binary embedded)
      ├── @charmland/crush-darwin-arm64 (binary embedded)
      └── ...
```

npm automatically installs only the matching platform package.

## Testing

The workflow can be triggered manually via `workflow_dispatch` or runs automatically on releases.

## References

- esbuild: https://github.com/evanw/esbuild
- opencode: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode  
- Issue discussion: #2230

title: fix(app): derive shutdown context from context.Background() instead of cancelled globalCtx
body:
- [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

When the user presses Ctrl+C, signal.NotifyContext cancels globalCtx. Shutdown() then derives shutdownCtx from it.

A child of a cancelled context is born cancelled, so the 5-second timeout never takes effect. All context-dependent cleanup silently short-circuits:
- shell.KillAll(shutdownCtx) — returns immediately, background shells not waited on
- mcp.Close(shutdownCtx) — returns immediately, MCP sessions not closed

## Fix
Use context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second) so shutdown cleanup gets a live 5-second window.

v1.3.1

This release is a patch release for v1.3.0.

It contains a cherry-pick for a security issue reported in #805, which takes advantage of the default behavior of Go's standard library JSON decoder that allows case-insensitive matches to struct field names (or "json" tags). The issue has been addressed by changing the JSON decoder to one that supports case sensitive matching.

Updates `modernc.org/sqlite` from 1.44.3 to 1.46.1
Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

  • 2026-02-17 v1.46.1:

    • Ensure connection state is reset if Tx.Commit fails. Previously, errors like SQLITE_BUSY during COMMIT could leave the underlying connection inside a transaction, causing errors when the connection was reused by the database/sql pool. The driver now detects this state and forces a rollback internally.
    • Fixes [GitHub issue #2](modernc-org/sqlite#2), thanks Edoardo Spadolini!

  • 2026-02-17 v1.46.0:

    • Enable ColumnTypeScanType to report time.Time instead of string for TEXT columns declared as DATE, DATETIME, TIME, or TIMESTAMP via a new _texttotime URI parameter.
    • See [GitHub pull request #1](modernc-org/sqlite#1), thanks devhaozi!

  • 2026-02-09 v1.45.0:

    • Introduce vtab subpackage (modernc.org/sqlite/vtab) exposing Module, Table, Cursor, and IndexInfo API for Go virtual tables.
    • Wire vtab registration into the driver: vtab.RegisterModule installs modules globally and each new connection calls sqlite3_create_module_v2.
    • Implement vtab trampolines for xCreate/xConnect/xBestIndex/xDisconnect/xDestroy/xOpen/xClose/xFilter/xNext/xEof/xColumn/xRowid.
    • Map SQLite’s sqlite3_index_info into vtab.IndexInfo, including constraints, ORDER BY terms, and constraint usage (ArgIndex → xFilter argv[]).
    • Add an in‑repo dummy vtab module and test (module_test.go) that validates registration, basic scanning, and constraint visibility.
    • See [GitLab merge request #90](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/90), thanks Adrian Witas!

title: fix(ui): optimize assistant message rendering to improve performance
body: This commit attempts to fix an issue where the rendering of assistant messages in the chat UI can become significantly degraded in performance, especially for long messages. The root cause of the performance degradation was identified as the use of lipgloss.Render for applying styles to the message content, which involves wrapping logic that can be expensive for long messages.

title: fix(lsp): prevent nil client from being stored in clients map
body: Fixes a nil pointer dereference panic (`SIGSEGV`) in `lsp.(*Manager).startServer` that occurs when an LSP server fails to spawn. `GetOrSet` unconditionally stored the return value of its callback into the clients map — even when `lsp.New()` returned `(nil, err)`. On any subsequent or concurrent call to `Start()`, the nil `*Client` was retrieved with `ok=true` and `GetServerState()` was called on it, causing the panic. Replaced `GetOrSet` with explicit Get/New/Set so that a nil client is never stored. Added a second Get-check before Set to handle the race where another goroutine successfully created the client in the meantime. - [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features).

title: refactor: improve code quality in internal/agent
body:
## Summary

This PR improves code quality in the `internal/agent` package through three key refactorings:

1. **Simplify context value retrieval using generics**
2. **Extract common sub-agent execution logic into `runSubAgent`**
3. **Use params struct to reduce parameter count and add unit tests**

## Changes

### 1. Context Value Retrieval Optimization

**Files**: `internal/agent/tools/tools.go`, `internal/agent/tools/context_test.go`

- Introduced generic `getContextValue` helper function
- Simplified each `Get*FromContext` function from ~13 lines to 2 lines
- Added comprehensive test coverage (18 test cases)
- Eliminated ~40 lines of duplicated nil checks and type assertions

**Before**:
```go
func GetSessionFromContext(ctx context.Context) string {
    sessionID := ctx.Value(SessionIDContextKey)
    if sessionID == nil {
        return ""
    }
    s, ok := sessionID.(string)
    if !ok {
        return ""
    }
    return s
}
```

**After**:
```go
func getContextValue[T any](ctx context.Context, key any, defaultValue T) T {
    value := ctx.Value(key)
    if value == nil {
        return defaultValue
    }
    if typedValue, ok := value.(T); ok {
        return typedValue
    }
    return defaultValue
}

func GetSessionFromContext(ctx context.Context) string {
    return getContextValue(ctx, SessionIDContextKey, "")
}
```

### 2. Sub-Agent Execution Logic Extraction

**Files**: `internal/agent/coordinator.go`, `internal/agent/agent_tool.go`, `internal/agent/agentic_fetch_tool.go`

- Added `subAgentParams` struct to replace 8 positional parameters (avoids misordering consecutive string args)
- Single `runSubAgent` method with optional `SessionSetup` callback field
- Added `updateParentSessionCost` helper for consistent cost propagation
- Improved error handling with proper error wrapping (`%w`)

**Before** (agent_tool.go — 59 lines of duplicated code):
```go
agentToolSessionID := c.sessions.CreateAgentToolSessionID(agentMessageID, call.ID)
session, err := c.sessions.CreateTaskSession(ctx, agentToolSessionID, sessionID, "New Agent Session")
if err != nil {
    return fantasy.ToolResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("error creating session: %s", err)
}
// ... 50+ more lines of session management, agent execution, cost propagation
```

**After**:
```go
return c.runSubAgent(ctx, subAgentParams{
    Agent:          agent,
    SessionID:      sessionID,
    AgentMessageID: agentMessageID,
    ToolCallID:     call.ID,
    Prompt:         params.Prompt,
    SessionTitle:   "New Agent Session",
})
```

For special cases with custom session setup (e.g. auto-approve):
```go
return c.runSubAgent(ctx, subAgentParams{
    // ...
    SessionSetup: func(sessionID string) {
        c.permissions.AutoApproveSession(sessionID)
    },
})
```

### 3. Unit Tests for `runSubAgent` and `updateParentSessionCost`

**File**: `internal/agent/coordinator_test.go`

12 test cases covering:

| Test | Scenario |
|------|----------|
| `TestRunSubAgent/happy_path` | Normal execution returns text response |
| `TestRunSubAgent/ModelCfg.MaxTokens_overrides_default` | MaxTokens precedence logic |
| `TestRunSubAgent/session_creation_failure` | Canceled context triggers error |
| `TestRunSubAgent/provider_not_configured` | Unknown provider returns error |
| `TestRunSubAgent/agent_run_error` | Agent failure returns error response (not Go error) |
| `TestRunSubAgent/session_setup_callback` | SessionSetup is invoked with correct session ID |
| `TestRunSubAgent/cost_propagation` | Child cost accumulates to parent session |
| `TestUpdateParentSessionCost/accumulates_cost` | Single child cost |
| `TestUpdateParentSessionCost/multiple_children` | Multiple child costs accumulate |
| `TestUpdateParentSessionCost/child_not_found` | Error on missing child session |
| `TestUpdateParentSessionCost/parent_not_found` | Error on missing parent session |
| `TestUpdateParentSessionCost/zero_cost` | Zero cost handled correctly |

## Testing

All existing and new tests pass:
```
ok  internal/agent       6.855s
ok  internal/agent/tools 6.283s
ok  internal/agent/tools/mcp (cached)
```

## Code Metrics

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
|--------|--------|-------|--------|
| tools.go | 75 lines | 56 lines | **-25.3%** |
| agent_tool.go | 106 lines | 67 lines | **-36.8%** |
| agentic_fetch_tool.go | 235 lines | 200 lines | **-14.9%** |
| Duplicated sub-agent code | 81 lines | 0 lines | **-100%** |
| Test coverage (coordinator) | 0 tests | 12 tests | **new** |

## Backward Compatibility

- No breaking changes to public APIs
- All existing tests pass
- Behavior remains identical

Updates `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` from 1.2.0 to 1.3.1
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk's releases.

v1.3.1

This release is a patch release for v1.3.0.

It contains a cherry-pick for a security issue reported in #805, which takes advantage of the default behavior of Go's standard library JSON decoder that allows case-insensitive matches to struct field names (or "json" tags). The issue has been addressed by changing the JSON decoder to one that supports case sensitive matching.

Fixes

  • all: use case-sensitive JSON unmarshaling by @​maciej-kisiel in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#807

New external dependencies

  • https://github.com/segmentio/encoding, which is the package that provides the new decoder.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/compare/v1.3.0...v1.3.1

v1.3.0

This release is equivalent to v1.3.0-pre.1. Thank you to those who tested the pre-release.

This release includes several enhancements and bugfixes. Worth mentioning is the addition of schema caching, which significantly improves the performance in some stateless server deployment scenarios.

Dependency updates

  • go.mod: upgrade to jsonschema v0.4.2 by @​jba in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#732

  • perf: add schema caching to avoid repeated reflection by @​SamMorrowDrums in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#685

title: UI renders duplicated content when streaming responses with code blocks (inherited from opencode)
body:
## Bug Description

When streaming LLM responses that contain code blocks (code fences, ASCII art, mermaid diagrams), the UI renders **massively duplicated content**. A ~150-line response balloons to **2,300+ lines** of visible duplicated text in the message thread.

## Environment

- **App:** opencode v1.2.10 (Mac desktop app) — filing here since opencode is archived and this codebase is the successor
- **OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon)
- **Model:** Claude Opus 4.6 via Amazon Bedrock

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open the app (TUI or desktop)
2. Send a prompt that generates a response containing multiple code fences, ASCII art, or mermaid diagram blocks
3. Observe the rendered output in the message thread

## Expected Behavior

Response renders once, ~150 lines, clean and readable.

## Actual Behavior

Content is duplicated dozens of times. Specific metrics from copy-pasting the rendered output:

- **Expected lines:** ~150
- **Actual lines:** 2,385
- **A single line** (`"Input:       2"`) appeared **78 times**

### Duplication Pattern

The duplication follows a specific pattern tied to streaming inside code blocks:

```
Line 90:  "w = 3              ← mermaid block cuts off mid-token
Line 91:  Input:       2      ← entire previous content re-renders from top
...
Line 132: flowchart TD        ← mermaid starts again
Line 138: "w = 3 ✓"]          ← gets further this time
...
Line 160: │  "                 ← ASCII box cuts off mid-character
Line 161: Input:       2      ← content re-renders AGAIN from top
```

Each time a new token arrives inside a code fence, the renderer appears to **re-emit all accumulated content** rather than appending the new token. Every re-render is captured as additional visible content in the message thread.

## Evidence

Full duplicated output file (2,385 lines from a ~150-line response): can be provided on request.

Screenshot showing the duplication visible in the desktop UI thread:

The user sees the same content blocks repeated dozens of times in the actual message thread, making responses unreadable.

## Impact

- Responses are completely unreadable due to duplicated content
- Copy-pasting from the thread gives 15-20x the actual content
- Any response with code blocks, ASCII art, or mermaid diagrams triggers this

## Likely Root Cause

The streaming markdown renderer re-renders the entire accumulated content block (not just the delta) on each token arrival inside code fences. This re-rendered content is being appended to the visible output instead of replacing the previous render.

title: Feature: Quick Quit Options for Shell (Linux/macOS)
body:
## Feature Request: Quick Quit Options for Crush Shell (Linux/macOS)

It would be great to have a simple and fast way to quit the Crush shell from any mode or dialog, especially when working on Linux or macOS. This could be a keyboard shortcut or menu action that immediately exits, even in cases where confirmation dialogs or busy states are active. This would streamline workflows and prevent unnecessary interruptions.

### Example Code References

#### Confirmation Dialog (Quit)
[internal/ui/dialog/quit.go](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/44f532e9f017e5feb9dc01d674da882ed0fbea90/internal/ui/dialog/quit.go) - Handles key bindings for quitting:
```go
// HandleMsg implements [Model].
func (q *Quit) HandleMsg(msg tea.Msg) Action {
	switch msg := msg.(type) {
	case tea.KeyPressMsg:
		switch {
		case key.Matches(msg, q.keyMap.Quit):
			return ActionQuit{}
		// ...
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

#### Keyboard Signal Handling (SIGINT/SIGTERM)
[internal/cmd/run.go](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/blob/44f532e9f017e5feb9dc01d674da882ed0fbea90/internal/cmd/run.go):
```go
ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, os.Kill)
defer cancel()
```

### Request
- Introduce a global keybinding (e.g., <kbd>Ctrl+Q</kbd>) or shell command for instant quit.
- Make sure this bypasses/handles confirmation dialogs and exits gracefully, even in interactive situations.
- Ensure compatibility with both Linux and macOS shells.
- Consider adding an environment variable such as `CRUSH_QUICK_QUIT_KEY` or similar, so users can customize or enable quick quit functionality.
- Allow quick quit keybinding to be set via environment variable/config file, for maximum flexibility across workflows.

This small improvement should make crushing workflows smoother and quicker for shell users!

Thank you for considering this feature. :)

title: Bug: Catwalk provider error wraps wrong variable — root cause always hidden as `<nil>`
body:
## Description

In `internal/config/provider.go`, the Catwalk provider error path wraps the **package-level** `providerErr` variable instead of the **local** `err` variable that contains the actual failure reason.

## Root Cause

```go
// internal/config/provider.go, inside Providers() -> sync.Once block

// line ~162
items, err := catwalkSyncer.Get(ctx)
if err != nil {
    // BUG: wraps `providerErr` (package-level var, nil at this point) instead of `err`
    errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("...Cause: %w", catwalkURL, providerErr))
}
```

At the time this code executes, `providerErr` is always `nil` because it's only assigned later (line ~189: `providerErr = errors.Join(errs...)`). Since this runs inside a `sync.Once`, `providerErr` from a "previous invocation" can never exist.

Compare with the **correct** pattern used for the Hyper provider on line ~180:

```go
errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("...Crush was unable to fetch updated information from Hyper: %w", err)) // correct: wraps local `err`
```

## Impact

When the Catwalk provider fetch fails (network error, auth failure, timeout), users see:

```
Crush was unable to fetch updated information from Catwalk. Cause: <nil>
```

instead of the actual error message. This makes debugging provider configuration issues extremely difficult — the real root cause is silently discarded.

## Expected Behavior

The error message should include the actual failure reason:

```
Crush was unable to fetch updated information from Catwalk. Cause: connection refused
```

## Proposed Fix

```diff
- errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("...Cause: %w", catwalkURL, providerErr))
+ errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("...Cause: %w", catwalkURL, err))
```

Note: The `//nolint:staticcheck` comment on the nearby line may have suppressed linter warnings that would have caught this.

## Willingness to Contribute

Happy to submit a PR for this one-line fix if the team agrees.

title: Bug: `os.Kill` (SIGKILL) passed to `signal.NotifyContext` — uncatchable signal, misleading graceful shutdown
body:
## Description

In `internal/cmd/run.go` (line ~44) and `internal/cmd/login.go` (line ~192), `os.Kill` is passed to `signal.NotifyContext`:

```go
ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, os.Kill)
```

`os.Kill` maps to `syscall.SIGKILL`, which **cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored** by any process — this is a POSIX guarantee. The Go documentation for `signal.Notify` explicitly states:

> SIGKILL and SIGSTOP may be registered but will not be delivered.

Passing `os.Kill` to `signal.NotifyContext` is a silent no-op. The context will never be cancelled by SIGKILL (the OS terminates the process immediately), but the code gives the false impression that graceful SIGKILL handling is implemented.

## Impact

- In `login.go`, a goroutine (line ~193) listens on `ctx.Done()` and calls `os.Exit(1)`. Since SIGKILL is uncatchable, this cleanup goroutine **never fires** on `kill -9`, meaning no cleanup runs despite being coded as if it would.
- In `run.go`, this represents misleading signal handling that could confuse future contributors into thinking SIGKILL is handled.
- The correct signal for "terminate gracefully" is `syscall.SIGTERM` (`os.Signal` value via `syscall.SIGTERM`), which IS catchable.

## Proposed Fix

Replace `os.Kill` with `syscall.SIGTERM`:

```diff
- ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, os.Kill)
+ ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
```

This correctly handles:
- `Ctrl+C` → `SIGINT` (`os.Interrupt`) ✅
- `kill <pid>` → `SIGTERM` (default signal) ✅
- `kill -9 <pid>` → `SIGKILL` (uncatchable, process dies immediately — correct behavior)

## Affected Files

- `internal/cmd/run.go`, line ~44
- `internal/cmd/login.go`, line ~192

## Willingness to Contribute

Happy to submit a PR for this fix across both files.

- Model: `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`
- Interface: `opencode web`

title: bug(lsp): applyTextEdit treats Position.Character as byte offset, breaks on non-ASCII content
body:
## Description

In `internal/lsp/util/edit.go`, `applyTextEdit()` directly uses `Position.Character` as a Go byte index to slice strings:

```go
startChar := int(edit.Range.Start.Character)
// ...
prefix := startLineContent[:startChar]
```

However, per the [LSP specification](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#position), `Position.Character` represents a **UTF-16 code unit offset**, not a byte offset. This causes incorrect edits (corrupted content or panics) on files containing non-ASCII characters such as CJK characters or emoji.

For example, given the line `var x = "你好world"`, an LSP server would report the `w` at Character 11 (UTF-16 units), but the actual byte offset in Go is 15 (each Chinese character is 3 UTF-8 bytes). Using 11 directly as a byte index slices into the middle of a multi-byte character.

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Implement UTF-16 to byte offset conversion

Add a conversion function in `applyTextEdit()` that translates UTF-16 code unit offsets to Go byte offsets before slicing strings. This correctly handles:

- CJK characters (1 UTF-16 unit → 3 UTF-8 bytes)
- Emoji / surrogate pairs (2 UTF-16 units → 4 UTF-8 bytes)

Pros: No dependency changes required.
Cons: Extra conversion on every edit; need to keep in sync if position encoding changes.

### Option 2: Negotiate UTF-8 position encoding with LSP servers

LSP 3.17 introduced [`general.positionEncodings`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#clientCapabilities) capability negotiation. If the client declares support for `utf-8` encoding, and the server agrees, then `Position.Character` becomes a **byte offset** directly — no conversion needed.

Currently, the powernap client hardcodes `"positionEncodings": ["utf-16"]` in `client.go:576`. Changing this to prefer `["utf-8", "utf-16"]` and respecting the server's negotiated encoding would eliminate the issue at its root.

Pros: Zero-cost at edit time; aligns naturally with Go's UTF-8 strings.
Cons: Requires changes to the powernap library; still needs a UTF-16 fallback for servers that don't support UTF-8.

## Recommendation

Option 2 (UTF-8 negotiation) is the cleaner long-term solution. Most modern LSP servers support UTF-8 encoding. A UTF-16 fallback (Option 1) can be added for completeness.

I can submit a PR to fix this.

title: Fix 800% CPU usage in large JS monorepo
body:
hasRootMarkers()  used  fsext.Glob()  to check for LSP root markers like  package.json  and  go.mod . Under the hood
this launched a recursive fastwalk of the entire working directory with no gitignore filtering, no  node_modules
skipping, and symlink following enabled. This ran every time an LSP server check was triggered (file reads, writes,
edits, session starts).

In large JS monorepos with deep  node_modules  trees, this walked millions of files/directories and consumed 97% of all
sampled CPU time across 8 cores.

Fix: Replace  fsext.Glob()  with  filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, pattern)) . Root markers are always simple filenames
or single-level wildcards ( go.mod ,  package.json ,  *.gpr ) that only exist at the project root — a recursive walk was
never needed.

Updates `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` from 1.3.1 to 1.4.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk's releases.

v1.4.0

This release marks the completion of the full 2025-11-25 specification implementation, by introducing the support for Sampling with Tools and experimental client-side OAuth support. It also contains multiple bug fixes and improvements. Thanks to all contributors!

Client-side OAuth support

This release introduces experimental support for OAuth on the client side of the SDK. It aims to support the full scope of the current MCP specification for authorization. To use it, you need to compile the SDK with the -tags mcp_go_client_oauth flag. Some changes may still be applied to this new API, based on developer feedback. The functionality is planned to become stable in v1.5.0 release, expected by the end of March 2026. More details can be found at https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/blob/main/docs/protocol.md#client.

  • all: client side OAuth support by @​maciej-kisiel in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#785

Sampling with Tools

Starting from this release, the server use the new CreateMessageWithTools method to create a sampling request to the client that contains tools that can be used by the client. On the client side, CreateMessageWithToolsHandler may be used to handle such requests and issue ToolUse responses to the server.

  • mcp: implement sampling with tools by @​findleyr in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#699

Behavior changes

We have two important behavior changes that were introduced to fix a bug or improve security posture. They can be temporarily turned off by specifying a special MCPGODEBUG environment variable when running the SDK. Different options can be added together, separated by a comma.

Introduced DNS rebinding protection (MCPGODEBUG=disablelocalhostprotection=1)

The requests arriving via a localhost address (127.0.0.1, [::1]) that have a non-localhost Host header will be rejected to protect against DNS rebinding attacks. The option to remove this protection will be removed in v1.6.0.

  • feat: add automatic DNS rebinding protection for localhost servers by @​pcarleton in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#760

Removed JSON content escaping when marshaling (MCPGODEBUG=jsonescaping=1):

By default encoding/json escapes the contents of the objects, which causes some servers to fail. We switched to no escaping by default. The option to bring back the escaping will be removed in v1.6.0.

  • mcp: update JSON marshaling to not HTML-escape messages by @​maciej-kisiel in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#769

Bug fixes

Security vulnerability caused by the case insensitive parsing behavior of encoding/json has been submitted (also release as a cherry pick in v1.3.1). Security advisory has been posted.

  • all: use case-sensitive JSON unmarshaling by @​maciej-kisiel in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#807

Other fixes:

  • mcp: validation only for accept action by @​CocaineCong in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#766
  • mcp: allow SSE messages with empty data (SEP-1699) by @​maciej-kisiel in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#779
  • jsonrpc2: fix Content-Length header parsing to be case-insensitive by @​nithinputhenveettil in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#789
  • mcp: fix multi-select enum elicitation by @​maciej-kisiel in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#795
  • mcp: return 400 instead of 500 when body read fails in stateless mode by @​roncodingenthusiast in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#817

Enhancements

Notably, the SDK now supports the extensions field in client and server capabilities, which should enable creation of MCP Apps.

  • mcp: add Extensions field to capabilities per SEP-2133 by @​ymmt2005 in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#794

Other enhancements:

  • mcp: export session missing error by @​CocaineCong in modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk#771

title: feat(commands): load Claude Code commands from .claude/commands
body:
## Summary

- Adds support for loading custom commands from Claude Code's `.claude/commands/` directories (`~/.claude/commands/` for global, `<project>/.claude/commands/` for project-level)
- Claude commands appear with a `claude:` prefix in the command palette alongside existing `user:` and `project:` commands
- YAML frontmatter (used by Claude Code for metadata) is automatically stripped from command content

## Motivation

Many developers use both Crush and Claude Code. Claude Code stores reusable prompt commands as `.md` files in `.claude/commands/` directories. This change lets Crush discover and use those same commands natively, so users can maintain a single set of commands that work across both tools.

The implementation is minimal — two new source directories in the existing command loading pipeline, a frontmatter stripping utility, and a `createDir` flag to avoid creating `.claude/` directories that don't already exist.

## Changes

**`internal/commands/commands.go`**:
- Added `claude:` command prefix and two new sources in `buildCommandSources()` for `~/.claude/commands/` (global) and `<project>/.claude/commands/` (project)
- Added `createDir` field to `commandSource` — Crush-native directories are created if missing; Claude directories are only read if they already exist
- Added `frontmatter` field to `commandSource` — when set, YAML frontmatter is stripped from command content before use
- Added `stripFrontmatter()` utility function

**`internal/commands/commands_test.go`** (new):
- Tests for frontmatter stripping (6 cases: no frontmatter, valid, empty, unclosed, multi-field, non-frontmatter dashes)
- Tests for loading Claude-format and Crush-format commands
- Tests for directory walking, missing directories, and source configuration

## Claude Code command format

```markdown
---
description: Review code changes
---
Review the code in $FILE and suggest improvements
```

The `$FILE` placeholder is automatically detected as a named argument by the existing `extractArgNames` logic — no special handling needed.

title: feat(agent): add toolcall detection wrapper for openai-compat provide…
body: ### Summary Local models served through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint put tool call JSON in the text content field instead of the structured `tool_calls` field. The fantasy library only reads `tool_calls`, so the JSON just shows up as plain text and tools never actually run. This PR adds a `LanguageModel` wrapper that intercepts text output from openai-compat providers, checks if it looks like tool call JSON with known tool names, and converts it into proper tool call events. ### What it handles - Raw JSON tool calls in text content - JSON wrapped in markdown code fences (`` ```json ... ``` ``) - Case-insensitive tool name matching (`View` → `view`) - Description-based aliases (`Read` → `view`, `Execute` → `bash`) - Stringified arguments (`"arguments": "{\"key\":\"value\"}"`) ### Files changed - `internal/agent/toolcall_detect.go` - the wrapper implementation - `internal/agent/toolcall_detect_test.go` - 50+ test cases - `internal/agent/coordinator.go` - wires up the wrapper for openai-compat providers ### Notes - Only wraps the large model (small model does summarization, no tool calling) - Rejects the entire batch if any tool name is unknown to avoid false positives - Tested end-to-end with `qwen2.5-coder:7b` on Ollama ### - [x] I have read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have created a discussion that was approved by a maintainer (for new features). ### Closes: #2073

title: feat: CLI-based session access and management
body:
Requires: https://github.com/charmbracelet/fang/pull/86 This revision adds a series of subcommands for CLI-based session inspection and management. All commands take `--json` flags machine-readable output. The goal here is to provide more programmatic, CLI-based access to Crush for non-interactive use cases. That said, while feature was primarily built for evaluations, but it has some user-facing details as well.

Listing sessions:

Viewing sessions:

UX notes: * Session are stored at UUIDs in the databases, however for ergonomics we're using hashes computed on the fly. Commands like `crush session show` can take either a UUID, hash, or partial hash like in git, i.e. `8a3173a`. In cases where a partial hash matches multiple items, Crush will error with a disambiguation message, similar to Git. * The pager will only be invoked in a TTY, and only when the height of the content is greater than the height of the terminal window. Colors will be stripped when output is not a TTY and, of course, machines will want to use `--json` anyway for all commands. * JSON output contains more data, such as including token spend and price in session output. *** This was built with GLM-5 and Kimi K2.5 in Crush.

## Summary

This PR introduces a comprehensive multi-agent orchestration system for Crush:

- **Orchestra**: A spec-driven multi-agent development system with hierarchical managers, GitHub integration, and git worktree isolation
- **Crush Instance Tool**: Spawns parallel Crush subprocesses for independent task execution with optional model selection
- **Dispatch System**: Database-backed dispatch service for task coordination
- **Spec Parser**: YAML-based specification parser and manager

### Orchestra System
- Spec-driven development with YAML specifications as single source of truth
- Hierarchical agent spawning and supervision
- GitHub integration (Issues, PRs, Milestones) for visibility

### Crush Instance Tool
- Spawn full Crush subprocesses for parallel task execution
- Optional model parameter to override default model per task
- Process lifecycle management (start, monitor, cleanup)
- UI components for displaying subprocess state

### Dispatch System
- SQLite-backed dispatch service
- Task queue management
- Support for task prioritization

title: feat(run): add session resume and JSON output for non-interactive mode
body:
## Summary

- Add `--session/-s` flag to continue an existing conversation in non-interactive mode
- Add `--output-format/-o` flag with `text` (default) and `json` options
- JSON output includes `session_id` and `result` fields for programmatic consumption
- Refactor `RunNonInteractive` to use `RunOptions`/`RunResult` structs for cleaner extensibility

## Use Cases

1. **Session resume**: Run a follow-up prompt in the same conversation context:
   ```bash
   # First run captures session_id
   crush run --output-format json "Analyze this code" | jq -r '.session_id'
   # Resume with that session
   crush run --session abc123 "Now add error handling"
   ```

2. **JSON output**: For CI/CD pipelines and scripting:
   ```bash
   crush run --output-format json "Generate tests" > result.json
   ```

- [x] `go test ./internal/cmd/... ./internal/app/...` - All tests pass

Sourced from charm.land/glamour/v2's releases.

v2.0.0

What's New in Glamour v2

We're excited to announce the second major release of Glamour!

If you (or your LLM) are just looking for technical details on migrating from v1, please check out the Upgrade Guide.

[!NOTE] We don't take API changes lightly and strive to make the upgrade process as simple as possible. We believe these changes bring necessary improvements and pave the way for the future. If something feels way off, let us know.

❤️ Charm Land Import Path

We've updated our import paths to use vanity domains and use our domain to import Go packages.

// Before
import "github.com/charmbracelet/glamour"

// After
import "charm.land/glamour/v2"

💄 Lip Gloss v2 Integration

Glamour v2 now uses Lip Gloss v2 under the hood, bringing improved performance and more consistent styling across the Charm ecosystem.

Since Glamour is designed to be pure (same input = same output), it doesn't peek at your terminal's capabilities. Instead, color downsampling is handled explicitly via Lip Gloss when you're ready to render:

r, _ := glamour.NewTermRenderer(glamour.WithWordWrap(80))
out, _ := r.Render(markdown)

// Downsample colors based on terminal capabilities
lipgloss.Print(out)

No more I/O fights between Glamour and Lip Gloss. Glamour focuses on rendering, Lip Gloss handles the colors. Everyone's happy!

🌏 Better Text Wrapping

Text wrapping has been rewritten using lipgloss.Wrap, which means way better handling of:

  • Multi-byte UTF-8 characters (CJK, emojis, etc.)
  • Complex Unicode sequences
  • Terminal cell width edge cases

Your Japanese documentation, emoji-filled READMEs, and creative Unicode art will all render beautifully now.
